name: Bench Jump
steps: Begin with a box or bench 1-2 feet in front of you. Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Perform a short squat in preparation for the jump; swing your arms behind you.
Rebound out of this position, extending through the hips, knees, and ankles to jump as high as possible. Swing your arms forward and up.
Jump over the bench, landing with the knees bent, absorbing the impact through the legs.
Turn around and face the opposite direction, then jump back over the bench.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Butt Lift (Bridge)
steps: Lie flat on the floor on your back with the hands by your side and your knees bent. Your feet should be placed around shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
Pushing mainly with your heels, lift your hips off the floor while keeping your back straight. Breathe out as you perform this part of the motion and hold at the top for a second.
Slowly go back to the starting position as you breathe in.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Double Leg Butt Kick
steps: Begin standing with your knees slightly bent.
Quickly squat a short distance, flexing the hips and knees, and immediately extend to jump for maximum vertical height.
As you go up, tuck your heels by flexing the knees, attempting to touch the buttocks.
Finish the motion by landing with the knees only partially bent, using your legs to absorb the impact.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Fast Skipping
steps: Start in a relaxed position with one leg slightly forward. This will be your starting position.
Skip by executing a step-hop pattern of right-right-step to left-left-step, and so on, alternating back and forth.
Perform fast skips by maintaining close contact with the ground and reduce air time, moving as quickly as possible.

name: Front Leg Raises
steps: Stand next to a chair or other support, holding on with one hand.
Swing your leg forward, keeping the leg straight. Continue with a downward swing, bringing the leg as far back as your flexibility allows. Repeat 5-10 times, and then switch legs.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Glute Kickback
steps: Kneel on the floor or an exercise mat and bend at the waist with your arms extended in front of you (perpendicular to the torso) in order to get into a kneeling push-up position but with the arms spaced at shoulder width. Your head should be looking forward and the bend of the knees should create a 90-degree angle between the hamstrings and the calves. This will be your starting position.

As you exhale, lift up your right leg until the hamstrings are in line with the back while maintaining the 90-degree angle bend. Contract the glutes throughout this movement and hold the contraction at the top for a second. Tip: At the end of the movement the upper leg should be parallel to the floor while the calf should be perpendicular to it.
Go back to the initial position as you inhale and now repeat with the left leg.
Continue to alternate legs until all of the recommended repetitions have been performed.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Groiners
steps: Begin in a pushup position on the floor. This will be your starting position.
Using both legs, jump forward landing with your feet next to your hands. Keep your head up as you do so.
Return to the starting position and immediately repeat the movement, continuing for 10-20 repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion

name: Hip Circles (Prone)
steps: Position yourself on your hands and knees on the ground. Maintaining good posture, raise one bent knee off of the ground. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the knee in a bent position, rotate the femur in an arc, attempting to make a big circle with your knee.
Perform this slowly for a number of repetitions, and repeat on the other side.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Knee Tuck Jump
steps: Begin in a comfortable standing position with your knees slightly bent. Hold your hands in front of you, palms down with your fingertips together at chest height. This will be your starting position.
Rapidly dip down into a quarter squat and immediately explode upward. Drive the knees towards the chest, attempting to touch them to the palms of the hands.
Jump as high as you can, raising your knees up, and then ensure a good land be re-extending your legs, absorbing impact through be allowing the knees to rebend.

name: Lateral Bound
steps: Assume a half squat position facing 90 degrees from your direction of travel. This will be your starting position.
Allow your lead leg to do a countermovement inward as you shift your weight to the outside leg.
Immediately push off and extend, attempting to bound to the side as far as possible.
Upon landing, immediately push off in the opposite direction, returning to your original start position.
Continue back and forth for several repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Lying Crossover
steps: Lie on your back with your legs extended.

Cross one leg over your body with the knee bent, attempting to touch the knee to the ground. Your partner should kneel beside you, holding your shoulder down with one hand and controlling the crossed leg with the other. this will be your starting position.
Attempt to raise the bent knee off of the ground as your partner prevents any actual movement.
After 10-20 seconds, relax the leg as your partner gently presses the knee towards the floor. Repeat with the other side.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Lying Glute
steps: Lie on your back with your partner kneeling beside you.

Flex the hip of one leg, raising it off of the floor. Rotate the leg so the foot is over the opposite hip, the lower leg perpendicular to your body. Your partner should hold the knee and ankle in place. This will be your starting position.
Attempt to push your leg towards your partner, who should be preventing any actual movement of the leg.

After 10-20 seconds, completely relax as your partner gently pushes the ankle and knee towards your chest. Be sure to inform your helper when the stretch is adequate to prevent injury or overstretching.

name: Lying Prone Quadriceps
steps: Lay face down on the floor with your partner kneeling beside you. Flex one knee and raise that leg off the ground, attempting to touch your glutes with your foot. Your partner should hold the knee and ankle. This will be your starting position.
Attempt to extend your knee while your partner prevents any actual movement.
After 10-20 seconds, relax your muscles as your partner gently pushes the foot towards your glutes, further stretching the quadriceps and hip flexors.
After 10-20 seconds, switch sides.

name: Natural Glute Ham Raise
steps: Using the leg pad of a lat pulldown machine or a preacher bench, position yourself so that your ankles are under the pads, knees on the seat, and you are facing away from the machine. You should be upright and maintaining good posture.
This will be your starting position. Lower yourself under control until your knees are almost completely straight.
Remaining in control, raise yourself back up to the starting position.
If you are unable to complete a rep, use a band, a partner, or push off of a box to aid in completing a repetition.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Rear Leg Raises
steps: Place yourself on your hands knees on an exercise mat. Your head should be looking forward and the bend of the knees should create a 90-degree angle between the hamstrings and the calves. This will be your starting position.
Extend one leg up and behind you. The knee and hip should both extend. Repeat for 5-10 repetitions, and then switch sides.

name: Rocket Jump
steps: Begin in a relaxed stance with your feet shoulder width apart and hold your arms close to the body.
To initiate the move, squat down halfway and explode back up as high as possible.
Fully extend your entire body, reaching overhead as far as possible. As you land, absorb your impact through the legs.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Scissors Jump
steps: Assume a lunge stance position with one foot forward with the knee bent, and the rear knee nearly touching the ground.
Ensure that the front knee is over the midline of the foot. Extending through both legs, jump as high as possible, swinging your arms to gain lift.
As you jump as high as you can, switch the position of your legs, moving your front leg to the back and the rear leg to the front.
As you land, absorb the impact through the legs by adopting the lunge position, and repeat.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Side Leg Raises
steps: Stand next to a chair, which you may hold onto as a support. Stand on one leg. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your leg straight, raise it as far out to the side as possible, and swing it back down, allowing it to cross the opposite leg.
Repeat this swinging motion 5-10 times, increasing the range of motion as you do so.

name: Single Leg Butt Kick
steps: Begin by standing on one leg, with the bent knee raised. This will be your start position.
Using a countermovement jump, take off upward by extending the hip, knee, and ankle of the grounded leg.
Immediately flex the knee and attempt to touch your butt with the heel of your jumping leg.
Return the leg to a partially bent position underneath the hips and land. Your opposite leg should stay in relatively the same position throughout the drill.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

steps: Lay on the floor with your feet flat and knees bent.
Raise one leg off of the ground, pulling the knee to your chest. This will be your starting position.
Execute the movement by driving through the heel, extending your hip upward and raising your glutes off of the ground.
Extend as far as possible, pause and then return to the starting position.

name: Standing Long Jump
steps: This drill is best done in sand or other soft landing surface. Ensure that you are able to measure distance. Stand in a partial squat stance with feet shoulder width apart.
Utilizing a big arm swing and a countermovement of the legs, jump forward as far as you can.
Attempt to land with your feet out in front you, reaching as far as possible with your legs.
Measure the distance from your landing point to the starting point and track results.

name: Step-Up With Knee Raise
steps: Stand facing a box or bench of an appropriate height with your feet together. This will be your starting position.

Begin the movement by stepping up, putting your left foot on the top of the bench. Extend through the hip and knee of your front leg to stand up on the box. As you stand on the box with your left leg, flex your right knee and hip, bringing your knee as high as you can.
Reverse this motion to step down off the box, and then repeat the sequence on the opposite leg.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

As you stand on the box with your left leg, flex your right knee and hip, bringing your knee as high as you can. name: Glute Bridge with Knee Lift
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, and arms resting along your sides.
Squeeze your glutes and push through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Holding your hips level and steady, lift your right foot off the floor and bring your knee toward your chest at a 90-degree angle.
Lower the right foot back down without allowing your pelvis to drop or rotate.
Repeat the march with your left foot while keeping your glutes engaged and hips elevated.
coaching_cues: Keep your pelvis level like a table; do not allow one hip to dip as you lift the opposite leg.
Lift with your glutes rather than arching with your lower back.
Take short, controlled breaths throughout.

Squeeze your glutes and push through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders. Holding your hips level and steady, lift your right foot off the floor and bring your knee toward your chest at a 90-degree angle. name: Side-Lying Leg Lift
steps: Lie on your side with your body in a straight line, resting your head on your bottom arm.
Keep your bottom leg slightly bent for stability and your top leg completely straight with toes pointed slightly downward.
Engage your outer hip and lift your top leg toward the ceiling roughly 45 degrees, leading with your heel.
Pause for one count at the top of the lift.
Slowly lower the leg back down without letting it rest heavily on the bottom leg.
coaching_cues: Keep your top hip tilted slightly forward to isolate the gluteus medius and prevent hip flexor dominance.
Lead with your heel, not your toes, to keep the outer hip engaged.
Avoid rolling backward onto your glutes.

steps: Lie on your side with your bottom leg straight and your head supported comfortably.
Cross your top leg over the bottom leg, placing the top foot flat on the floor in front of your bottom knee.
Keep your bottom leg straight and flex your bottom foot.
Lift the bottom leg upward toward the ceiling a few inches, squeezing your inner thigh muscles.
Hold for one second at the top, then slowly lower the leg back down without touching the floor.
coaching_cues: Focus on lifting with your inner thigh rather than swinging the leg.
Keep your pelvis steady and avoid rocking backward.
Breathe out as you lift the leg and breathe in as you lower.

name: Donkey Kick
steps: Start on hands and knees with your shoulders over wrists and hips over knees.
Brace your core to keep your spine completely neutral throughout the exercise.
Keeping your right knee bent at a 90-degree angle, lift your right leg behind you, pressing the sole of your foot toward the ceiling.
Squeeze your glute firmly at the top of the movement, ensuring your lower back does not arch.
Slowly lower the knee back down without touching the floor, completing all reps before switching sides.
coaching_cues: The movement should come purely from the hip joint, not from sagging or arching your lower back.
Keep your neck neutral with your eyes looking down at the mat between your hands.
Push the floor away with your hands to keep your shoulders stable.

Keeping your right knee bent at a 90-degree angle, lift your right leg behind you, pressing the sole of your foot toward the ceiling. name: Fire Hydrant
steps: Begin on all fours on a comfortable mat with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keep your core engaged and your weight evenly distributed across both hands.
Maintaining a 90-degree bend in your right knee, lift your right leg out to the side like a dog at a fire hydrant.
Lift only as high as you can without tilting your pelvis or shifting your torso to the left.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower your knee back to the starting position.
coaching_cues: Resist the urge to lean your body weight heavily toward the supporting side.
Focus on contracting the outer glute and hip rotators.
Keep your spine neutral throughout the repetition.

Lift only as high as you can without tilting your pelvis or shifting your torso to the left. Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower your knee back to the starting position.

name: Supine Hip Cross-Over Stretch
steps: Lie flat on your back with legs extended straight.
Bend your right knee and place your right foot on the outside of your left thigh or knee.
Use your left hand to gently guide your right knee across your body toward the floor on your left side.
Extend your right arm straight out to the right, keeping your right shoulder blade in contact with the mat.
Hold the gentle stretch in your outer hip and glute for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing deeply, then switch sides.
coaching_cues: Do not force your knee all the way to the floor; listen to your body and stop at a gentle stretch.
Keep your right shoulder grounded on the floor.
Relax your neck and jaw as you breathe.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with legs extended straight. Bend your right knee and place your right foot on the outside of your left thigh or knee. Use your left hand to gently guide your right knee across your body toward the floor on your left side. Extend your right arm straight out to the right, keeping your right shoulder blade in contact with the mat. Hold the gentle stretch in your outer hip and glute for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing deeply, then switch sides.

name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
steps: Kneel on a soft exercise mat and step your right foot forward so your right knee is bent at 90 degrees directly above your ankle.
Keep your torso upright with hands on your front thigh or hips.
Gently tuck your pelvis under (posterior pelvic tilt) and squeeze your left glute to engage the front of your left hip.
Shift your weight slightly forward while keeping your chest tall until you feel a deep, gentle stretch in the front of your left hip and thigh.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then switch legs.
coaching_cues: Avoid hyperextending your lower back; the stretch comes from tucking the pelvis and squeezing the rear glute.
Place an extra towel or pillow under the back knee if you experience joint discomfort.
Breathe deeply and sink comfortably into the stretch.
instructions: Kneel on a soft exercise mat and step your right foot forward so your right knee is bent at 90 degrees directly above your ankle. Keep your torso upright with hands on your front thigh or hips. Gently tuck your pelvis under (posterior pelvic tilt) and squeeze your left glute to engage the front of your left hip. Shift your weight slightly forward while keeping your chest tall until you feel a deep, gentle stretch in the front of your left hip and thigh. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then switch legs.

name: Reverse Lunge with Overhead Reach
steps: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms hanging at your sides.
Step your right foot straight backward and lower your body into a reverse lunge until both knees are bent at roughly 90 degrees.
As you sink into the lunge, reach both arms overhead and slightly backward, opening up your chest and the front of your right hip.
Lower your arms as you push through your front left heel to return to the standing position.
Repeat the movement by stepping back with your left foot.
coaching_cues: A reverse lunge places significantly less shear stress on the front knee than a forward lunge.
Keep your front knee stacked over your front ankle without caving inward.
Inhale as you step back and reach overhead; exhale as you return to stand.
instructions: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms hanging at your sides. Step your right foot straight backward and lower your body into a reverse lunge until both knees are bent at roughly 90 degrees. As you sink into the lunge, reach both arms overhead and slightly backward, opening up your chest and the front of your right hip. Lower your arms as you push through your front left heel to return to the standing position. Repeat the movement by stepping back with your left foot.

name: Lateral Lunge with Pause

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: NASM Frontal Plane Functional Movement Training

steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands clasped comfortably in front of your chest.
Take a wide step to your right, keeping both feet pointed straight ahead.
Hinge your hips back and bend your right knee, lowering into a side lunge while keeping your left leg completely straight.
Pause at the bottom of the lunge for two full seconds, feeling a deep stretch along the inside of your straight left leg.
Push strongly off your right foot to return to the center standing position, then repeat to the left.
coaching_cues: Keep the heel of your lunging foot firmly planted on the floor throughout.
Send your hips backward as if sitting into a chair behind your lunging leg.
Maintain an upright chest and open posture.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands clasped comfortably in front of your chest. Take a wide step to your right, keeping both feet pointed straight ahead. Hinge your hips back and bend your right knee, lowering into a side lunge while keeping your left leg completely straight. Pause at the bottom of the lunge for two full seconds, feeling a deep stretch along the inside of your straight left leg. Push strongly off your right foot to return to the center standing position, then repeat to the left.

name: Bodyweight Good Morning
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees soft (slightly unlocked).
Place your fingertips gently behind your head with elbows opened wide.
Keeping your spine long and chest open, push your hips straight backward as if touching a wall behind you.
Hinge forward from your hips until your torso is roughly 45 to 60 degrees forward and you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Squeeze your glutes and push your hips forward to return to an upright standing posture.
coaching_cues: This is a hip hinge, not a squat; your shins should stay vertical as your hips travel backward.
Do not round your shoulders or pull on your neck.
Keep your weight balanced through your midfoot and heels.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees soft (slightly unlocked). Place your fingertips gently behind your head with elbows opened wide. Keeping your spine long and chest open, push your hips straight backward as if touching a wall behind you. Hinge forward from your hips until your torso is roughly 45 to 60 degrees forward and you feel a stretch in your hamstrings. Squeeze your glutes and push your hips forward to return to an upright standing posture.

name: Inchworm Walkout
steps: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
Hinge at your hips and bend forward, placing your hands flat on the floor in front of your feet (soften knees if needed).
Walk your hands forward one at a time across the floor until your body reaches a full, straight high plank position.
Pause in the high plank for one full second with your core tightly engaged.
Walk your hands backward toward your feet, keeping your legs as straight as comfortable, and return to a standing position.
coaching_cues: Maintain steady core tension in the plank; do not allow your lower back or hips to sag.
Keep your hands under your shoulders as you walk forward.
Breathe naturally throughout the walkout.
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides. Hinge at your hips and bend forward, placing your hands flat on the floor in front of your feet (soften knees if needed). Walk your hands forward one at a time across the floor until your body reaches a full, straight high plank position. Pause in the high plank for one full second with your core tightly engaged. Walk your hands backward toward your feet, keeping your legs as straight as comfortable, and return to a standing position.

name: Wall Sit

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: British Journal of Sports Medicine Isometric Tendon Protocol

steps: Stand with your back flat against a smooth wall, with your feet shoulder-width apart and roughly 2 feet out from the wall.
Slide your back down the wall until your thighs are nearly parallel to the floor and your knees are bent at roughly 90 degrees.
Ensure your knees are directly above your ankles, not extending past your toes.
Press your entire back and shoulders firmly into the wall and rest your hands on your hips or crossed over your chest.
Hold this isometric position for the desired duration while breathing calmly, then slide back up.
coaching_cues: Beginners can start at a higher angle (45 to 60 degrees) and gradually slide deeper as strength builds.
Do not rest your hands on your knees to support your weight.
Drive your heels down into the floor to keep tension distributed between quads and glutes.
instructions: Stand with your back flat against a smooth wall, with your feet shoulder-width apart and roughly 2 feet out from the wall. Slide your back down the wall until your thighs are nearly parallel to the floor and your knees are bent at roughly 90 degrees. Ensure your knees are directly above your ankles, not extending past your toes. Press your entire back and shoulders firmly into the wall and rest your hands on your hips or crossed over your chest. Hold this isometric position for the desired duration while breathing calmly, then slide back up.

name: Tandem Heel-to-Toe Walk

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: CDC STEADI Balance Training & Otago Exercise Programme

steps: Stand tall near a wall or countertop so you have a support surface within reach if needed.
Place the heel of your right foot directly in front of the toes of your left foot, touching or nearly touching.
Focus your eyes on a fixed point on the wall ahead to help maintain stability.
Take a step forward with your left foot, placing your left heel directly in front of your right toes.
Continue stepping forward in a straight line for 10 to 15 deliberate steps.
coaching_cues: Keep your arms outstretched to your sides like a tightrope walker if helpful for balance.
Move with slow, deliberate precision rather than rushing forward.
Stand as tall as possible through your crown.
instructions: Stand tall near a wall or countertop so you have a support surface within reach if needed. Place the heel of your right foot directly in front of the toes of your left foot, touching or nearly touching. Focus your eyes on a fixed point on the wall ahead to help maintain stability. Take a step forward with your left foot, placing your left heel directly in front of your right toes. Continue stepping forward in a straight line for 10 to 15 deliberate steps.

name: Single-Leg Balance Stand

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: APTA Ankle Sprain Clinical Practice Guidelines

steps: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart near a sturdy surface or wall.
Shift your weight onto your left foot, keeping your standing knee soft and unlocked.
Lift your right foot off the floor, bending the right knee to roughly 90 degrees.
Keep your hips level and gaze focused on a stable point straight ahead.
Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then gently lower your foot and repeat on the right leg.
coaching_cues: Keep your standing foot firmly rooted with equal pressure across your big toe, pinky toe, and heel.
Keep a light fingertip on the wall if you feel unsteady.
To increase difficulty as you advance, try crossing your arms over your chest or closing your eyes.
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart near a sturdy surface or wall. Shift your weight onto your left foot, keeping your standing knee soft and unlocked. Lift your right foot off the floor, bending the right knee to roughly 90 degrees. Keep your hips level and gaze focused on a stable point straight ahead. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then gently lower your foot and repeat on the right leg.

name: Standing Calf Toe Raise

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: NIH Senior Health & Physical Function Standards

steps: Stand tall facing a wall or the back of a sturdy chair with feet hip-width apart.
Place your fingertips lightly on the support surface for balance.
Slowly raise your heels off the floor, pressing evenly through the balls of both feet until you are standing high on your toes.
Pause at the top for one full second, feeling your calf muscles fully contract.
Slowly lower your heels back down to the floor under control.
coaching_cues: Push straight up through your big toes rather than rolling your weight to the outside edges of your feet.
Do not lean your upper body forward onto the support surface.
Maintain smooth, continuous movement on both the ascent and descent.
instructions: Stand tall facing a wall or the back of a sturdy chair with feet hip-width apart. Place your fingertips lightly on the support surface for balance. Slowly raise your heels off the floor, pressing evenly through the balls of both feet until you are standing high on your toes. Pause at the top for one full second, feeling your calf muscles fully contract. Slowly lower your heels back down to the floor under control.

name: Clamshell
steps: Lie on your side with your head resting on your bottom arm, stacking your hips and shoulders in a straight vertical line.
Bend your knees to a 90-degree angle and bend your hips to approximately 45 degrees, with your feet stacked together.
Keeping your heels glued together, slowly rotate your top knee upward toward the ceiling as high as comfortable without rolling your pelvis backward.
Pause at the top for one full second, feeling your outer glute contract.
Slowly lower your top knee back down until it touches your bottom knee.
coaching_cues: Place your top hand on your hip bone to verify your pelvis stays still and does not rock backward.
Only raise the knee as high as you can maintain pure hip rotation.
Keep your feet touching throughout the entire set.
instructions: Lie on your side with your head resting on your bottom arm, stacking your hips and shoulders in a straight vertical line. Bend your knees to a 90-degree angle and bend your hips to approximately 45 degrees, with your feet stacked together. Keeping your heels glued together, slowly rotate your top knee upward toward the ceiling as high as comfortable without rolling your pelvis backward. Pause at the top for one full second, feeling your outer glute contract. Slowly lower your top knee back down until it touches your bottom knee.

name: Straight Leg Raise
steps: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your left knee bent and left foot flat on the floor.
Extend your right leg straight out on the floor and flex your right foot upward.
Tighten the muscles on top of your right thigh so your knee is completely locked straight.
Maintaining that quad lock, lift your right leg roughly 12 inches off the floor until your thigh is parallel with your bent left thigh.
Hold for one to two seconds at the top, then slowly lower the straight leg back down to the floor.
coaching_cues: Your knee must stay completely straight during the entire lift; do not allow it to bend.
Keep your lower back flat on the mat without arching.
Perform smoothly and steadily without kicking.
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your left knee bent and left foot flat on the floor. Extend your right leg straight out on the floor and flex your right foot upward. Tighten the muscles on top of your right thigh so your knee is completely locked straight. Maintaining that quad lock, lift your right leg roughly 12 inches off the floor until your thigh is parallel with your bent left thigh. Hold for one to two seconds at the top, then slowly lower the straight leg back down to the floor.

name: Hip 90-90 Mobility Stretch
steps: Sit on the floor with your front right leg bent at a 90-degree angle directly in front of you, shin perpendicular to your torso.
Position your rear left leg bent at a 90-degree angle out to the left, shin pointing backward.
Sit as tall as possible with your spine upright, using hands on the floor for balance if necessary.
Gently hinge forward from your hips over your front right shin until you feel a deep stretch in your right outer hip.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, sit back upright, switch your legs to the opposite side, and repeat.
coaching_cues: Do not slouch through your lower back; think of leading forward with your sternum.
If your back hip feels pinched, place a yoga block or pillow under your front hip.
Breathe slowly and deeply to encourage tissue relaxation.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your front right leg bent at a 90-degree angle directly in front of you, shin perpendicular to your torso. Position your rear left leg bent at a 90-degree angle out to the left, shin pointing backward. Sit as tall as possible with your spine upright, using hands on the floor for balance if necessary. Gently hinge forward from your hips over your front right shin until you feel a deep stretch in your right outer hip. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, sit back upright, switch your legs to the opposite side, and repeat.

name: Wall Gastrocnemius Stretch

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: Cornell Health Lower Extremity ROM Protocol

steps: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away and place both palms flat against the wall at shoulder height.
Step your target leg backward, keeping that back leg completely straight with the heel firmly on the ground.
Bend your front knee and gently lean your hips forward toward the wall.
Maintain the straight back leg and flat heel until you feel a comfortable stretch in the upper half of your back calf.
Hold steady for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing deeply, then switch legs.
coaching_cues: Keep your back foot pointing directly forward toward the wall; do not let your toes flare outward.
Keep your back heel glued firmly to the floor throughout the stretch.
Maintain an upright posture without slouching through your lower back.
instructions: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away and place both palms flat against the wall at shoulder height. Step your target leg backward, keeping that back leg completely straight with the heel firmly on the ground. Bend your front knee and gently lean your hips forward toward the wall. Maintain the straight back leg and flat heel until you feel a comfortable stretch in the upper half of your back calf. Hold steady for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing deeply, then switch legs.

name: Wall Soleus Stretch

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: Cornell Health Lower Extremity ROM Protocol

steps: Stand facing a wall with hands resting flat against the wall for support.
Step your target leg back slightly, about 6 to 12 inches behind your front foot.
Unlike the standard calf stretch, bend both knees and sink your hips straight downward toward the floor.
Keep your back heel pressed down on the floor as you bend your back knee deeper.
Feel a deep, focused stretch in the lower portion of your calf and Achilles tendon, holding for 20 to 30 seconds.
coaching_cues: Bending the knee takes tension off the gastrocnemius to isolate the deeper soleus muscle.
Keep your weight distributed evenly and do not let your back heel lift.
Breathe comfortably and allow the lower calf to release.
instructions: Stand facing a wall with hands resting flat against the wall for support. Step your target leg back slightly, about 6 to 12 inches behind your front foot. Unlike the standard calf stretch, bend both knees and sink your hips straight downward toward the floor. Keep your back heel pressed down on the floor as you bend your back knee deeper. Feel a deep, focused stretch in the lower portion of your calf and Achilles tendon, holding for 20 to 30 seconds.

name: Wall Heel Slide
steps: Lie on your back with your glutes near a wall and legs resting vertically up against the wall.
Slowly slide the heel of your target leg downward along the wall, bending your knee as far as comfortably tolerated.
Let gravity assist the gentle bending of your knee into a pain-free stretch.
Pause at your maximum comfortable bend for 2 to 3 seconds.
Contract your quad and slide your heel back up the wall to the straight-leg starting position.
coaching_cues: Wear a sock or place a small towel under your heel so it glides smoothly on the wall.
You can use your opposite foot to lightly support or guide the target foot if needed.
Never force into sharp joint pain; allow gentle progressive stretching.
instructions: Lie on your back with your glutes near a wall and legs resting vertically up against the wall. Slowly slide the heel of your target leg downward along the wall, bending your knee as far as comfortably tolerated. Let gravity assist the gentle bending of your knee into a pain-free stretch. Pause at your maximum comfortable bend for 2 to 3 seconds. Contract your quad and slide your heel back up the wall to the straight-leg starting position.

name: Prone Knee Flexion

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: Cornell Health Lower Extremity ROM Protocol

steps: Lie face down on a mat with your legs extended straight and forehead resting comfortably on your hands.
Keep your pelvis pressed gently into the mat so your lower back does not arch.
Slowly bend your target knee, drawing your heel toward your glute through a full, comfortable range of motion.
Pause for one second at the top of the curl, engaging your hamstring muscles.
Slowly lower your foot back down to the floor under control.
coaching_cues: Keep your hips flat on the mat; do not lift your hip as your knee bends.
Perform smoothly without swinging or kicking.
Focus on a clean, active contraction of the hamstring.
instructions: Lie face down on a mat with your legs extended straight and forehead resting comfortably on your hands. Keep your pelvis pressed gently into the mat so your lower back does not arch. Slowly bend your target knee, drawing your heel toward your glute through a full, comfortable range of motion. Pause for one second at the top of the curl, engaging your hamstring muscles. Slowly lower your foot back down to the floor under control.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: Cornell Health Lower Extremity Strengthening Protocol

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
Extend one leg straight out in line with your opposite thigh, or bend it toward your chest.
Press firmly down through the heel of your grounded foot and squeeze your glute to lift your hips off the mat.
Lift until your body forms a straight line from your grounded knee through your hips to your shoulder.
Pause at the top for one second with your hips level, then slowly lower back to the mat.
coaching_cues: Do not allow your pelvis to drop or rotate toward the non-working side.
Drive purely through the heel of the working leg to maximize glute contraction.
Keep your neck and upper shoulders relaxed on the mat.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart. Extend one leg straight out in line with your opposite thigh, or bend it toward your chest. Press firmly down through the heel of your grounded foot and squeeze your glute to lift your hips off the mat. Lift until your body forms a straight line from your grounded knee through your hips to your shoulder. Pause at the top for one second with your hips level, then slowly lower back to the mat.

name: Supine Hip Internal Rotation Stretch

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: Cornell Health Lower Extremity Range of Motion Protocol

steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, placed slightly wider than hip-width apart.
Keeping your left knee pointing up, slowly let your right knee drop inward toward the floor and toward your left ankle.
Keep both shoulder blades and your lower back resting comfortably on the mat.
Feel a gentle stretch in the outer hip and front of your right hip joint.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, return the right knee upright, and repeat with the left leg.
coaching_cues: Do not force your knee to touch the floor; allow gravity to create a gentle, comfortable stretch.
If you experience sharp pinching inside the hip joint, stop the stretch immediately.
Breathe slowly and rhythmically.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, placed slightly wider than hip-width apart. Keeping your left knee pointing up, slowly let your right knee drop inward toward the floor and toward your left ankle. Keep both shoulder blades and your lower back resting comfortably on the mat. Feel a gentle stretch in the outer hip and front of your right hip joint. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, return the right knee upright, and repeat with the left leg.

name: Supine Hip External Rotation Stretch

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: Cornell Health Lower Extremity Range of Motion Protocol

steps: Lie comfortably on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Bring the soles of your feet together and slowly allow both knees to fall open to the sides toward the floor.
Rest your hands gently on your lower abdomen or alongside your body.
Feel a gentle, relaxing stretch through your inner thighs and groin.
Hold the position for 30 to 45 seconds while focusing on deep abdominal breathing.
coaching_cues: Place yoga blocks or pillows under your outer thighs if the stretch feels too intense on your groin.
Do not arch your lower back aggressively off the floor.
Relax your inner thighs completely with each exhalation.
instructions: Lie comfortably on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Bring the soles of your feet together and slowly allow both knees to fall open to the sides toward the floor. Rest your hands gently on your lower abdomen or alongside your body. Feel a gentle, relaxing stretch through your inner thighs and groin. Hold the position for 30 to 45 seconds while focusing on deep abdominal breathing.

name: Seated Long Arc Quad
steps: Sit tall on a sturdy chair or examination table with your back supported and your knees bent at 90 degrees.
Rest your hands comfortably on your thighs or grip the sides of the seat for stability.
Slowly lift your target foot and straighten your leg out in front of you until your knee is fully extended and parallel to the floor.
Flex your ankle toward your shin and squeeze your quadriceps firmly at the top for 2 to 3 seconds.
Slowly lower your foot back down under control until it gently touches the floor.
coaching_cues: Maintain an upright posture and avoid slouching or leaning back as your leg straightens.
Move smoothly without kicking or swinging using momentum.
Control the downward lowering phase over 2 full seconds.
instructions: Sit tall on a sturdy chair or examination table with your back supported and your knees bent at 90 degrees. Rest your hands comfortably on your thighs or grip the sides of the seat for stability. Slowly lift your target foot and straighten your leg out in front of you until your knee is fully extended and parallel to the floor. Flex your ankle toward your shin and squeeze your quadriceps firmly at the top for 2 to 3 seconds. Slowly lower your foot back down under control until it gently touches the floor.

name: Prone Straight Leg Raise
steps: Lie face down (prone) on a mat with your legs extended straight and your forehead resting on your folded hands.
Tighten your abdominal muscles slightly to brace your lower back and keep your pelvis anchored to the floor.
Squeeze your glute on the target side and lift your entire straight leg roughly 4 to 6 inches off the floor.
Ensure your knee remains locked straight and your hip bone stays in contact with the mat.
Hold for 2 seconds at the peak of the lift, focusing on glute contraction.
Slowly lower your leg back down to the floor under control.
coaching_cues: Do not arch your lower back or twist your hips to lift the leg higher; motion should come purely from the glute.
Keep your toes pointed down toward the floor.
Maintain steady abdominal bracing to protect your lumbar spine.
instructions: Lie face down (prone) on a mat with your legs extended straight and your forehead resting on your folded hands. Tighten your abdominal muscles slightly to brace your lower back and keep your pelvis anchored to the floor. Squeeze your glute on the target side and lift your entire straight leg roughly 4 to 6 inches off the floor. Ensure your knee remains locked straight and your hip bone stays in contact with the mat. Hold for 2 seconds at the peak of the lift, focusing on glute contraction. Slowly lower your leg back down to the floor under control.

name: Ankle Pumps

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: AAOS Foot and Ankle Conditioning Program

steps: Sit or lie comfortably with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Point your toes and feet forward away from your body as far as possible, as if depressing a car accelerator pedal.
Hold for 1 second in full plantarflexion.
Pull your toes and feet backward toward your shins into full dorsiflexion.
Hold for 1 second in dorsiflexion, feeling the calf and shin muscles alternately engage.
Continue pumping rhythmically between pointing and flexing for the prescribed repetitions.
coaching_cues: Move strictly through your ankle joints while keeping your knees and hips still.
Perform smooth, rhythmic pumps to promote circulation and venous blood return.
Work through full available pain-free range of motion.
instructions: Sit or lie comfortably with your legs extended straight in front of you. Point your toes and feet forward away from your body as far as possible, as if depressing a car accelerator pedal. Hold for 1 second in full plantarflexion. Pull your toes and feet backward toward your shins into full dorsiflexion. Hold for 1 second in dorsiflexion, feeling the calf and shin muscles alternately engage. Continue pumping rhythmically between pointing and flexing for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Ankle Alphabet

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: AAOS Foot and Ankle Conditioning Program

steps: Sit comfortably on a chair with your leg lifted off the floor or resting on your opposite knee.
Imagine your big toe is a pen or pencil pointing forward.
Trace each capital letter of the alphabet in the air from A to Z using only your ankle and foot.
Make the letters as large as comfortable to move through all ranges of motion: dorsiflexion, plantarflexion, inversion, and eversion.
Complete the alphabet on one foot, then switch to the other side.
coaching_cues: Isolate the movement to the ankle joint; do not rotate your whole leg from the knee or hip.
Trace both small curves and wide angles deliberately.
Take your time with letters like S, W, and Z that require multiplanar coordination.
instructions: Sit comfortably on a chair with your leg lifted off the floor or resting on your opposite knee. Imagine your big toe is a pen or pencil pointing forward. Trace each capital letter of the alphabet in the air from A to Z using only your ankle and foot. Make the letters as large as comfortable to move through all ranges of motion: dorsiflexion, plantarflexion, inversion, and eversion. Complete the alphabet on one foot, then switch to the other side.

name: Heel Walking

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: AAOS Foot and Ankle Conditioning Program

steps: Stand tall in a clear hallway or open room with good posture.
Lift your toes and the balls of both feet off the floor, balancing entirely on your heels.
Keep your ankles strongly dorsiflexed with your toes pulled high toward your shins.
Take small, controlled steps forward on your heels while maintaining your balance.
Walk forward for the designated duration or distance without letting your toes touch the ground.
coaching_cues: Stay tall with your chest up; avoid hunching your back or sticking your hips excessively backward.
Keep your toes lifted high throughout every single step to fire the anterior shin muscles.
Walk near a wall or railing if you need balance support.
instructions: Stand tall in a clear hallway or open room with good posture. Lift your toes and the balls of both feet off the floor, balancing entirely on your heels. Keep your ankles strongly dorsiflexed with your toes pulled high toward your shins. Take small, controlled steps forward on your heels while maintaining your balance. Walk forward for the designated duration or distance without letting your toes touch the ground.

name: Toe Walking

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: AAOS Foot and Ankle Conditioning Program

steps: Stand upright in an open space with your feet hip-width apart.
Rise up as high as possible onto the balls of your feet and toes, lifting your heels completely off the ground.
Take small, steady steps forward while maintaining maximum height on your toes.
Walk for the prescribed duration or distance, keeping your calves contracted continuously.
coaching_cues: Stay tall and maintain an engaged core for balance.
Do not allow your ankles to roll outward; keep weight evenly distributed across the balls of your feet and big toes.
Breathe evenly throughout the walk.
instructions: Stand upright in an open space with your feet hip-width apart. Rise up as high as possible onto the balls of your feet and toes, lifting your heels completely off the ground. Take small, steady steps forward while maintaining maximum height on your toes. Walk for the prescribed duration or distance, keeping your calves contracted continuously.

name: Cable Deadlift
steps: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend at the hips and knees, lowering your torso until your back is parallel to the ground.
Grasp the cable handles with an overhand grip, keeping your arms straight and your shoulders back.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift the cable handles, extending your hips and standing up straight.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the cable handles back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Bend at the hips and knees, lowering your torso until your back is parallel to the ground. Grasp the cable handles with an overhand grip, keeping your arms straight and your shoulders back. Engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift the cable handles, extending your hips and standing up straight. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the cable handles back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Cable Hip Adduction
steps: Attach the ankle cuff to your ankle and stand facing the cable machine.
Position yourself far enough away from the machine so that there is tension on the cable.
Place your hands on the machine for support.
Keeping your leg straight, slowly move your leg across your body towards the midline.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Attach the ankle cuff to your ankle and stand facing the cable machine. Position yourself far enough away from the machine so that there is tension on the cable. Place your hands on the machine for support. Keeping your leg straight, slowly move your leg across your body towards the midline. name: Dumbbell Seated One Leg Calf Raise - Hammer Grip
steps: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the ground and a dumbbell resting on your thighs.
Place one foot on a raised surface, such as a step or block, with your heel hanging off the edge.
Hold the dumbbell with a hammer grip, meaning your palms are facing each other and your fingers are wrapped around the handle.
Keeping your core engaged and your back straight, slowly raise your heel as high as possible by pushing through the ball of your foot.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, hinge at the hips and lower the dumbbells towards the ground, allowing your knees to bend slightly.
Lower the dumbbells until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, then push through your heels and engage your glutes to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Deadlift
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand.
Shift your weight onto your left leg and lift your right foot slightly off the ground.
Keeping your back straight, hinge forward at the hips and lower the dumbbell towards the ground.
At the same time, extend your right leg straight behind you, maintaining a slight bend in your left knee.
Lower the dumbbell until your torso and right leg are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then engage your glutes and hamstrings to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, lower your body down into a squat position by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Farmers Walk
steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your sides.
Keep your back straight and your shoulders back.
Take small, controlled steps forward, maintaining an upright posture.
Continue walking for the desired distance or time.
To finish, stop walking and carefully lower the dumbbells to your sides.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up Lunge
steps: Stand in front of a step or platform with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your sides.
Place your right foot on the step, ensuring your entire foot is on the surface.
Push through your right heel and lift your body up onto the step, bringing your left foot up as well.
Once both feet are on the step, lower your left foot back down to the starting position, keeping your right foot on the step.
Repeat the movement, alternating which foot you step up with each time.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions.

Keeping your chest up and core engaged, slowly lower your body down by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Deadlift With Stepbox Support
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand.
Place your left foot on a stepbox or elevated surface behind you.
Keeping your back straight and core engaged, hinge forward at the hips, lowering the dumbbell towards the ground.
As you lower the dumbbell, simultaneously lift your left leg behind you, maintaining a straight line from head to heel.
Lower the dumbbell until you feel a stretch in your right hamstring, then return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Pull Through
steps: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointed outwards.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands in front of your body, arms extended.
Bend your knees and lower your hips down into a squat position, keeping your back straight.
Lower the dumbbell down between your legs, keeping your arms straight.
Drive through your heels and extend your hips forward, pulling the dumbbell up and in front of your body.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement, then lower the dumbbell back down between your legs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up Split Squat

Place your right foot on the bench or step, ensuring your entire foot is in contact with the surface.
Step up onto the bench or step with your right foot, pushing through your heel to lift your body up.
As you step up, simultaneously lift your left knee towards your chest.
Pause at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your left foot back to the ground while keeping your right foot on the bench or step.
Repeat the movement with your left foot on the bench or step.
Continue alternating between your right and left foot for the desired number of repetitions.

steps: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and toes pointing slightly outward.
Hold a weight in front of your chest with both hands.
Shift your weight to one side and lower your body by bending the knee of the side you shifted towards, while keeping the other leg straight.
Go as low as you can while maintaining balance and keeping your chest up.
Push through the heel of the bent leg to return to the starting position.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight in each hand.
Take a step forward with your right foot, lowering your body into a lunge position.
As you lunge forward, swing the weights forward and upward, keeping your arms straight.
Push off with your right foot and return to the starting position, swinging the weights back down.
Repeat with your left foot and continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Snatch
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand with an overhand grip.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Lower the dumbbell towards the ground, keeping it close to your body.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles, driving the dumbbell upwards in a straight line.
As the dumbbell reaches shoulder height, quickly rotate your hand and punch it overhead, fully extending your arm.
Catch the dumbbell overhead with a slight bend in your knees and hips.
Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

As the dumbbell reaches shoulder height, quickly rotate your hand and punch it overhead, fully extending your arm. Catch the dumbbell overhead with a slight bend in your knees and hips. Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position in a controlled manner. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

name: Dumbbell Lunges
steps: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. This will be your starting position.

Step forward with your right leg around 2 feet or so from the foot being left stationary behind and lower your upper body down, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance. Inhale as you go down. Note: As in the other exercises, do not allow your knee to go forward beyond your toes as you come down, as this will put undue stress on the knee joint. Make sure that you keep your front shin perpendicular to the ground.
Using mainly the heel of your foot, push up and go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat the movement for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Dumbbell Seated Box Jump
steps: Position a box a couple feet to the side of a bench. Hold a dumbbell to your chest with both hands and seat yourself on the bench facing the box. This will be your starting position.
Plant your feet firmly on the ground as you lean forward, extending through the hips and knees to jump up and forward.
Land on the box with both feet, absorbing the impact by allowing the hips and knees to bend.
Step down and return to the starting position.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Dumbbell Squat To A Bench
steps: Stand up straight with a flat bench behind you while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).

Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances discussed in the foot stances section.

Begin to slowly lower your torso by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until you slightly touch the bench behind you. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Dumbbell Step Ups
steps: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).

Place the right foot on the elevated platform. Step on the platform by extending the hip and the knee of your right leg. Use the heel mainly to lift the rest of your body up and place the foot of the left leg on the platform as well. Breathe out as you execute the force required to come up.

Step down with the left leg by flexing the hip and knee of the right leg as you inhale. Return to the original standing position by placing the right foot of to next to the left foot on the initial position.
Repeat with the right leg for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Plie Dumbbell Squat
steps: Hold a dumbbell at the base with both hands and stand straight up. Move your legs so that they are wider than shoulder width apart from each other with your knees slightly bent.
Your toes should be facing out. Note: Your arms should be stationary while performing the exercise. This is the starting position.
Slowly bend the knees and lower your legs until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Make sure to inhale as this is the eccentric part of the exercise.
Press mainly with the heel of the foot to bring the body back to the starting position while exhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion

name: Split Squat With Dumbbells
steps: Position yourself into a staggered stance with the rear foot elevated and front foot forward.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, letting them hang at the sides. This will be your starting position.
Begin by descending, flexing your knee and hip to lower your body down. Maintain good posture througout the movement. Keep the front knee in line with the foot as you perform the exercise.
At the bottom of the movement, drive through the heel to extend the knee and hip to return to the starting position.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Vertical Swing
steps: Allow the dumbbell to hang at arms length between your legs, holding it with both hands. Keep your back straight and your head up.
Swing the dumbbell between your legs, flexing at the hips and bending the knees slightly.
Powerfully reverse the motion by extending at the hips, knees, and ankles to propel yourself upward, swinging the dumbell over your head.
As you land, absorb the impact through your legs and draw the dumbbell to your torso before the next repetition.

Drive through your heels to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.

name: Calf Press On The Leg Press Machine
steps: Using a leg press machine, sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a medium (shoulder width) foot stance.

Lower the safety bars holding the weighted platform in place and press the platform all the way up until your legs are fully extended in front of you without locking your knees. (Note: In some leg press units you can leave the safety bars on for increased safety. If your leg press unit allows for this, then this is the preferred method of performing the exercise.) Your torso and the legs should make perfect 90-degree angle. Now carefully place your toes and balls of your feet on the lower portion of the platform with the heels extending off. Toes should be facing forward, outwards or inwards as described at the beginning of the chapter. This will be your starting position.

Press on the platform by raising your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position by a second before you start to go back down.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Leg Extensions
steps: For this exercise you will need to use a leg extension machine. First choose your weight and sit on the machine with your legs under the pad (feet pointed forward) and the hands holding the side bars. This will be your starting position. Tip: You will need to adjust the pad so that it falls on top of your lower leg (just above your feet). Also, make sure that your legs form a 90-degree angle between the lower and upper leg. If the angle is less than 90-degrees then that means the knee is over the toes which in turn creates undue stress at the knee joint. If the machine is designed that way, either look for another machine or just make sure that when you start executing the exercise you stop going down once you hit the 90-degree angle.
Using your quadriceps, extend your legs to the maximum as you exhale. Ensure that the rest of the body remains stationary on the seat. Pause a second on the contracted position.
Slowly lower the weight back to the original position as you inhale, ensuring that you do not go past the 90-degree angle limit.
Repeat for the recommended amount of times.

As you exhale, curl your legs up as far as possible without lifting the upper legs from the pad. Once you hit the fully contracted position, hold it for a second.

name: Lying Machine Squat
steps: Adjust the leg machine to a height that will allow you to get inside it with your knees bent and the thighs slightly below parallel.

Once you select the weight, position yourself inside the machine face up with the knees bent and thighs slightly below parallel to the platform. Make sure that the knees do not go past the toes. The angle created between the hamstrings and the calves should be one that is slightly less than 90 degrees (since your starting position requires you to start slightly below parallel). Your back and your head should be resting on the machine while your shoulders are pressed under the shoulder pads.
Place your hands by the handles and position your feet slightly pointing out at a shoulder width position. This will be your starting position.

While pressing with the balls of the feet as you breathe out, make your whole body erect as you squeeze the quads. Hold the contracted position for a second. Tip: Since you are starting below parallel, you can opt to use your hands to help you up by pressing on your thighs only on the first repetition.

Slowly squat down as you inhale but instead of going all the way down to the starting position, just stop once your thighs are parallel to the platform. The angle between your hamstrings and calves should be a 90-degree angle.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Smith Machine Hang Power Clean

Take a pronated grip on the bar outside of shoulder width and unhook the bar from the machine. Your arms should be fully extended with your head and chest up. Initate the movement by forcefully extending the hips and knees, accelerating into the bar. Ensure that you keep your arms straight during this part of the motion.
Upon full extension, rebend the hips and knees to lower your receiving position.

steps: To begin, sit down on the adductor machine and select a weight you are comfortable with. When your legs are positioned properly on the leg pads of the machine, grip the handles on each side. Your entire upper body (from the waist up) should be stationary. This is the starting position.
Slowly press against the machine with your legs to move them towards each other while exhaling.

Feel the contraction for a second and begin to move your legs back to the starting position while breathing in. Note: Remember to keep your upper body stationary and avoid fast jerking motions in order to prevent any injuries from occurring.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and the trap bar on the ground in front of you.
Bend at the hips and knees to lower yourself down and grip the handles of the trap bar with an overhand grip.
Keep your back straight and chest up as you begin to lift the trap bar off the ground by extending your hips and knees.
As you lift, focus on driving through your heels and squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Lower the trap bar back down to the ground by bending at the hips and knees, keeping your back straight throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Roller Hip Stretch
steps: Start by sitting on the ground with your legs extended in front of you.
Place the roller under your glutes, just above your knees.
Lean back and place your hands on the ground behind you for support.
Engage your glutes and slowly roll the roller forward, bending your knees and bringing them towards your chest.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, feeling a stretch in your glutes.
Slowly roll the roller back to the starting position, extending your legs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then roll back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Tire Flip
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the tire.
Bend your knees and hinge at the hips, lowering into a squat position.
Reach down and grab the bottom edge of the tire with both hands, fingers facing towards you.
Engage your glutes and leg muscles, and explosively drive through your legs to lift the tire off the ground.
As the tire flips over, use your upper body strength to guide it and maintain control.
Once the tire is fully flipped, quickly step back and reset your stance.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Adductor/Groin
steps: Lie on your back with your feet raised towards the ceiling.
Have your partner hold your feet or ankles. Abduct your legs as far as you can. This will be your starting position.
Attempt to squeeze your legs together for 10 or more seconds, while your partner prevents you from doing so.

Now, relax the muscles in your legs as your partner pushes your feet apart, stretching as far as is comfortable for you. Be sure to let your partner know when the stretch is adequate to prevent overstretching or injury.

name: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound
steps: Assume a comfortable stance with one foot slightly in front of the other.
Begin by pushing off with the front leg, driving the opposite knee forward and as high as possible before landing. Attempt to cover as much distance to each side with each bound.
It may help to use a line on the ground to guage distance from side to side.
Repeat the sequence with the other leg.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Ankle On The Knee
steps: From a lying position, bend your knees and keep your feet on the floor.

Grasp the thigh or knee of the bottom leg and pull both of your legs into the chest. Relax your neck and shoulders. Hold for 10-20 seconds and then switch sides.

name: Anterior Tibialis-SMR
steps: Begin seated on the ground with your legs bent and your feet on the floor.

Using a Muscle Roller or a rolling pin, apply pressure to the muscles on the outside of your shins. Work from just below the knee to above the ankle, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat on the other leg.

name: Backward Drag

name: Bench Sprint
steps: Stand on the ground with one foot resting on a bench or box with your heel close to the edge.
Push off with your foot on top of the bench, extending through the hip and knee.
Land with the opposite foot on top of the box, returning your other foot back to the start position.
Continue alternating from one foot to another to complete the set.

name: Bodyweight Walking Lunge
steps: Begin standing with your feet shoulder width apart and your hands on your hips.

Step forward with one leg, flexing the knees to drop your hips. Descend until your rear knee nearly touches the ground. Your posture should remain upright, and your front knee should stay above the front foot.
Drive through the heel of your lead foot and extend both knees to raise yourself back up.
Step forward with your rear foot, repeating the lunge on the opposite leg.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Box Jump (Multiple Response)
steps: Assume a relaxed stance facing the box or platform approximately an arm's length away. Arms should be down at the sides and legs slightly bent.
Using the arms to aid in the initial burst, jump upward and forward, landing with feet simultaneously on top of the box or platform.
Immediately drop or jump back down to the original starting place; then repeat the sequence.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Box Skip
steps: You will need several boxes lined up about 8 feet apart.
Begin facing the first box with one leg slightly behind the other.
Drive off the back leg, attempting to gain as much height with the hips as possible.

Immediately upon landing on the box, drive the other leg forward and upward to gain height and distance, leaping from the box. Land between the first two boxes with the same leg that landed on the first box.
Then, step to the next box and repeat.

name: Calf Stretch Elbows Against Wall

Lean against the wall, placing your weight on your forearms.
Attempt to keep your heels on the ground. Hold for 10-20 seconds. You may move further or closer the wall, making it more or less difficult, respectively.

name: Calves-SMR
steps: Begin seated on the floor. Place a foam roller underneath your lower leg. Your other leg can either be crossed over the opposite or be placed on the floor, supporting some of your weight. This will be your starting position.

Place your hands to your side or just behind you, and press down to raise your hips off of the floor, placing much of your weight against your calf muscle. Roll from below the knee to above the ankle, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat for the other leg.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Car Deadlift
steps: This event apparatus typically has neutral grip handles, however some have a straight bar that you can approach like a normal deadlift. The apparatus can be loaded with a vehicle or other heavy objects such as tractor tires or kegs.

Center yourself between the handles if you are a strong squatter, or back a couple inches if you are a strong deadlifter. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hip to grip the handles. With your feet and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and flex the knees.

Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back arched, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward. As the weight comes up, pull your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward.
Lower the weight by bending at the hips and guiding it to the floor.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Carioca Quick Step
steps: Begin with your feet a few inches apart and your left arm up in a relaxed, athletic position.
With your right foot, quick step behind and pull the knee up.
Fire your arms back up when you pull the right knee, being sure that your knee goes straight up and down. Avoid turning your feet as you move and continue to look forward as you move to the side.

name: Conan'S Wheel
steps: With the weight loaded, take a zurcher hold on the end of the implement. Place the bar in the crook of the elbow and hold onto your wrist. Try to keep the weight off of the forearms.

Begin by lifting the weight from the ground. Keep a tight, upright posture as you being to walk, taking short, fast steps. Look up and away as you turn in a circle. Do not hold your breath during the event. Continue walking until you complete one or more complete turns.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Depth Jump Leap
steps: For this drill you will need two boxes or benches, one 12 to 16 inches high and the other 22 to 26 inches high.

Stand on one of the two boxes with arms at the sides; feet should be together and slightly off the edge as in the depth jump. Place the other box approximately two or three feet in front of and facing the performer.
Begin by dropping off the initial box, landing and simultaneously taking off with both feet.
Rebound by driving upward and outward as intensely as possible, using the arms and full extension of the body to jump onto the higher box. Again, allow the legs to absorb the impact.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Donkey Calf Raises
steps: For this exercise you will need access to a donkey calf raise machine. Start by positioning your lower back and hips under the padded lever provided. The tailbone area should be the one making contact with the pad.

Place both of your arms on the side handles and place the balls of your feet on the calf block with the heels extending off. Align the toes forward, inward or outward, depending on the area you wish to target, and straighten the knees without locking them. This will be your starting position.

Raise your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position by a second before you start to go back down.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
