steps: You can use a partner for this exercise or brace your feet under something stable.
Begin on your knees with your upper legs and torso upright. If using a partner, they will firmly hold your feet to keep you in position. This will be your starting position.
Lower yourself by extending at the knee, taking care to NOT flex the hips as you go forward.

Place your hands in front of you as you reach the floor. This movement is very difficult and you may be unable to do it unaided. Use your arms to lightly push off the floor to aid your return to the starting position.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Foot-SMR
steps: This exercise stretches the fascia of the muscles in the feet. Start off seated with your shoes removed. Using a foot roller or a similar object, such as a small section of pvc pipe, place your foot against the roller across the arch of your foot. This will be your starting position.
Press down firmly, rolling across the arch of your foot. Hold for 10-30 seconds, and then switch feet.

name: Frog Hops
steps: Stand with your hands behind your head, and squat down keeping your torso upright and your head up. This will be your starting position.
Jump forward several feet, avoiding jumping unnecessarily high. As your feet contact the ground, absorb the impact through your legs, and jump again. Repeat this action 5-10 times.

name: Front Box Jump
steps: Begin with a box of an appropriate height 1-2 feet in front of you. Stand with your feet should width apart. This will be your starting position.
Perform a short squat in preparation for jumping, swinging your arms behind you.
Rebound out of this position, extending through the hips, knees, and ankles to jump as high as possible. Swing your arms forward and up.
Land on the box with the knees bent, absorbing the impact through the legs. You can jump from the box back to the ground, or preferably step down one leg at a time.

Stand in front of the first cone with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.

Absorb the impact of landing by bending the knees, rebounding out of the first leap by jumping over the next cone.

name: Knee Across The Body
steps: Lie down on the floor with your right leg straight. Bend your left leg and lower it across your body, holding the knee down toward the floor with your right hand. (The knee doesn't need to touch the floor if you're tight.)

Place your left arm comfortably beside you and turn your head to the left. Imagine you have a weight tied to your tailbone. let your tailbone fall back toward the floor as your chest reaches in the opposite direction to stretch your lower back. Switch sides.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Kneeling Hip Flexor
steps: Kneel on a mat and bring your right knee up so the bottom of your foot is on the floor and extend your left leg out behind you so the top of your foot is on the floor.
Shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch in your hip. Hold for 15 seconds, then repeat for your other side.

name: Lateral Box Jump
steps: Assume a comfortable standing position, with a short box positioned next to you. This will be your starting position.
Quickly dip into a quarter squat to initiate the stretch reflex, and immediately reverse direction to jump up and to the side.
Bring your knees high enough to ensure your feet have good clearance over the box.
Land on the center of the box, using your legs to absorb the impact.
Carefully jump down to the other side of the box, and continue going back and forth for several repetitions.

Stand next to the end of the cones, facing 90 degrees to the direction of travel. This will be your starting position.
Begin the jump by dipping with the knees to initiate a stretch reflex, and immediately reverse direction to push off the ground, jumping up and sideways over the cone.
Use your legs to absorb impact upon landing, and rebound into the next jump, continuing down the row of cones.

name: Linear 3-Part Start Technique
steps: This drill helps you accelerate as quickly as possible into a sprint from a dead stop. It helps to use a line to start from. Begin with two feet on the line. Place your left foot with the toe next to your right ankle. Place your right foot 4-6 inches behind the left.
Place your right hand onto the line, and thing bring your nose close to your left knee.
Squat down as you lean foward, your head being lower than your hips and your weight loaded onto the left leg. This will be your starting position.
Take your left hand up so that it is parallel to the ground, pointing behind you, and explode out when ready.

name: Linear Acceleration Wall Drill
steps: Lean at around 45 degrees against a wall. Your feet should be together, glutes contracted.
Begin by lifting your right knee quickly, pausing, and then driving it straight down into the ground.
Switch legs, raising the opposite knee, and then attacking the ground straight down.
Repeat once more with your right leg, and as soon as the right foot strikes the ground hammer them out rapidly, alternating left and right as fast as you can.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Linear Depth Jump
steps: You will need two boxes or benches spaced a few feet away from each other. Begin by standing on one box facing towards the other platform.
To initiate the movement, gently drop down to the ground between your platforms, allowing the knees and hips to flex.
Reverse the motion by exploding, extending through the hips, knees, and ankles to jump onto the other platform.
Land softly, asborbing the impact through the legs.

name: Looking At Ceiling

Lift your buttocks up and forward while bringing your head back to look up at the ceiling, to give an arch in your back.

name: Lying Bent Leg Groin
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and the soles of the feet pressed together. Have your partner hold your knees. This will be your starting position.
Attempt to squeeze your knees together, while your partner prevents any movement from occurring.
After 10-20 seconds, relax your muscles as your partner gently pushes your knees towards the floor. Be sure to inform your helper when the stretch is adequate to prevent injury or overstretching.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Lying Hamstring
steps: Lie on your back with your legs extended. Your partner should be kneeling beside you. Raise one leg up towards the ceiling and have your partner hold the ankle. Your partner can use their shoulder to brace your leg if necessary. This will be your starting position.
With your partner holding your leg in place, attempt to flex the knee, contracting the hamstrings for 10-20 seconds.

Then relax your leg, allowing your partner to gently push the leg towards your head. Be sure to inform your helper when the stretch is adequate to prevent injury or overstretching. Switch sides once complete.

name: Mountain Climbers
steps: Begin in a pushup position, with your weight supported by your hands and toes. Flexing the knee and hip, bring one leg until the knee is approximately under the hip. This will be your starting position.

Explosively reverse the positions of your legs, extending the bent leg until the leg is straight and supported by the toe, and bringing the other foot up with the hip and knee flexed. Repeat in an alternating fashion for 20-30 seconds.

Pull the belly button to the spine to stay in neutral. Press your foot down and into your hand. To add the hip stretch, lift the hip of the leg you're holding up toward the ceiling.
Switch sides.

name: One Half Locust
steps: Lie facedown on the floor.
Put your left hand under your left hipbone to pad your hip and pubic bone.
Bend your right knee so you can hold the foot in your right hand.

Lift the foot in the air and simultaneously lift your shoulders off the floor. This also stretches the right hip flexor and the chest and shoulders. Switch sides. If it doesn't bother your back, you can try it with both arms and legs at the same time.

Extend one leg straight and pull the other knee to your chest. Hold under the knee joint to protect the kneecap.

Begin the movement by flexing the knee, keeping your other leg straight.
Continue bringing the heel closer to you, sliding it on the floor.
At full knee flexion, reverse the movement to return to the starting position.

name: Power Stairs
steps: In the power stairs, implements are moved up a staircase. For training purposes, these can be performed with a tire or box.

Begin by taking the implement with both hands. Set your feet wide, with your head and chest up. Drive through the ground with your heels, extending your knees and hips to raise the weight from the ground.
As you lean back, attempt to swing the weight onto the stairs, which are usually around 16-18" high. You can use your legs to help push the weight onto the stair.
Repeat for 3-5 repetitions, and continue with a heavier weight, moving as fast as possible.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Rickshaw Deadlift
steps: Load the frame with the desired weight. Center yourself between the handles. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hips to grip the handles, allowing your shoulder blades to protract.

With your feet and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and flex the knees. Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back arched, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward. As the weight comes up, pull your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward.
Lower the weight by bending at the hips and guiding it to the ground.

Keep the front heel on the floor (if it lifts up, scoot your other leg further back).

Place your hands on either side of your front leg. To get more out of this stretch, push your butt up toward the ceiling, and then gradually lower it back toward the floor. You'll Stretch the hip flexor of the back leg and the hamstring and buttocks of the front.

name: Sandbag Load
steps: To load sandbags or other objects, begin with the implements placed a distance from the loading platform, typically 50 feet.

Begin by lifting the sandbag. Sandbags are extremely awkward, and the manner of lifting them can vary depending on the particular sandbag used. Reach as far around it as possible, extending through the hips and knees to pull it up high. Shouldering is usually not allowed.
Move as quickly as possible to the platform, and load it, extending through your hips, knees, and ankles to get it as high as possible. Place it onto the platform, ensuring it doesn't fall off.
Return to the starting position to retrieve the next sandbag, and repeat until the event is completed.

Leaning to your right, extend through your hips, knees, and ankles to jump into the air. Block with the arms to lead the movement, jumping as far to your right as you can. Land facing the same direction with your feet hip width apart, absorbing the impact through your lower body.

name: Side To Side Box Shuffle
steps: Stand to one side of the box with your left foot resting on the middle of it.
To begin, jump up and over to the other side of the box, landing with your right foot on top of the box and your left foot on the floor. Swing your arms to aid your movement.
Continue shuffling back and forth across the box.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

To begin, jump up and over to the other side of the box, landing with your right foot on top of the box and your left foot on the floor. Swing your arms to aid your movement. name: Single-Cone Sprint Drill
steps: This drill teaches quick foot action. You need a single cone. Begin standing next to the cone with one arm back and one arm forward.
Chop the feet as quickly as possible, blocking with the arms. Circle the cone, keep your knees up, with violent foot action.
Rest after three trips around the cone.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

Chop the feet as quickly as possible, blocking with the arms. Circle the cone, keep your knees up, with violent foot action. Rest after three trips around the cone.

name: Single-Leg High Box Squat
steps: Position a box in a rack. Secure a band or rope in place above the box.
Standing in front of it, step onto the box to a full standing position, letting your other leg remain unsupported. Hold onto the band for balance
. Continue stepping up and down on the same leg before switching to the opposite side.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Single-Leg Hop Progression
steps: Arrange a line of cones in front of you. Assume a relaxed standing position, balanced on one leg. Raise the knee of your opposite leg. This will be your starting position.
Hop forward, jumping and landing with the same leg over the cone.
Use a countermovement jump to hop from cone to cone.
At the end, turn around and go back on the other leg.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Single-Leg Lateral Hop
steps: Stand to the side of a cone or hurdle. To get into the start position, stand on one leg with your knee slightly bent.
To begin, execute a counterjump to hop sideways over the cone.
Land on your jumping leg, and immediately rebound out of it by jumping back to the start position.
Continue hopping back and forth.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

Land on your jumping leg, and immediately rebound out of it by jumping back to the start position. Continue hopping back and forth.

name: Single-Leg Stride Jump
steps: Stand to the side of a box with your inside foot on top of it, close to the edge.
Begin by swinging the arms upward as you push through the top leg, jumping upward as high as possible. Attempt to drive the opposite knee upward.
Land in the same position that you started, using your inside leg to decelerate the impact.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

Attempt to drive the opposite knee upward. Land in the same position that you started, using your inside leg to decelerate the impact.

name: Single Leg Push-Off
steps: Stand on the ground with one foot resting on the box, heel close to the edge.
Push off with your foot on top of the box, trying to gain as much height as possible by extending through the hip and knee.
Land with the same foot on top of the box, returning your other foot back to the start position.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

Push off with your foot on top of the box, trying to gain as much height as possible by extending through the hip and knee. name: Sit Squats
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Begin the movement by flexing your knees and hips, sitting back with your hips.
Continue until you have squatted a portion of the way down, but are above parallel, and quickly reverse the motion until you return to the starting position. Repeat for 5-10 repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

Continue until you have squatted a portion of the way down, but are above parallel, and quickly reverse the motion until you return to the starting position. Repeat for 5-10 repetitions.

name: Sled Drag - Harness
steps: To begin, load the sled with the desired weight and attach the pulling strap. You can pull with handles, use a harness, or attach the pulling strap to a weight belt.
Whether pulling forwards or backwards, lean in the direction of travel and progress by extending through the hips and knees.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Sled Push
steps: Load your pushing sled with the desired weight.

Take an athletic posture, leaning into the sled with your arms fully extended, grasping the handles. Push the sled as fast as possible, focusing on extending your hips and knees to strengthen your posterior chain.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Standing Elevated Quad Stretch
steps: Start by standing with your back about two to three feet away from a bench or step.
Lift one leg behind you and rest your foot on the step,either on your instep or the ball of your foot, whichever you find most comfortable.
Keep your supporting knee slightly bent and avoid letting that knee extend out beyond your toes. Switch sides.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

Lift one leg behind you and rest your foot on the step,either on your instep or the ball of your foot, whichever you find most comfortable. Keep your supporting knee slightly bent and avoid letting that knee extend out beyond your toes. Switch sides.

name: Standing Hip Flexors
steps: Stand up straight with the spine vertical, the left foot slightly in front of the right.

Bend both knees and lift the back heel off the floor as you press the right hip forward. You can't get a thorough, deep stretch in this position, however, because it's hard to relax the hip flexor and stand on it at the same time. Switch sides.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

You can't get a thorough, deep stretch in this position, however, because it's hard to relax the hip flexor and stand on it at the same time. Switch sides.

name: Standing Soleus And Achilles Stretch
steps: Stand with your feet hip-distance apart, one foot slightly in front of the other.
Bend both knees, keeping your back heel on the floor. Switch sides.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-distance apart, one foot slightly in front of the other. Bend both knees, keeping your back heel on the floor. Switch sides.

name: Standing Toe Touches
steps: Stand with some space in front and behind you.
Bend at the waist, keeping your legs straight, until you can relax and let your upper body hang down in front of you. Let your arms and hands hang down naturally. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Stand with some space in front and behind you. Bend at the waist, keeping your legs straight, until you can relax and let your upper body hang down in front of you. Let your arms and hands hang down naturally. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds.

name: Stride Jump Crossover
steps: Stand to the side of a box with your inside foot on top of it, close to the edge.
Begin by swinging the arms upward as you push through the top leg, jumping upward as high as possible. Attempt to drive the opposite knee upward.
Land in the opposite position that you started, on the opposite side of the box. The foot that was initially on the box will now be on the ground, with the opposite foot now on the box.
Repeat the movement, crossing back over to the other side.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Stand to the side of a box with your inside foot on top of it, close to the edge. Begin by swinging the arms upward as you push through the top leg, jumping upward as high as possible. Attempt to drive the opposite knee upward. Land in the opposite position that you started, on the opposite side of the box. The foot that was initially on the box will now be on the ground, with the opposite foot now on the box. Repeat the movement, crossing back over to the other side.

name: The Straddle
steps: Begin in a seated, upright position. Start by extending your legs in front of you in a V.
With your hands on the floor, lean forward as far as possible. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Begin in a seated, upright position. Start by extending your legs in front of you in a V. With your hands on the floor, lean forward as far as possible. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds.

name: Upper Back-Leg Grab
steps: While seated, bend forward to hug your thighs from underneath with both arms.
Keep your knees together and your legs extended out as you bring your chest down to your knees. You can also stretch your middle back by pulling your back away from your knees as your hugging them.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: While seated, bend forward to hug your thighs from underneath with both arms. Keep your knees together and your legs extended out as you bring your chest down to your knees. You can also stretch your middle back by pulling your back away from your knees as your hugging them.

name: Windmills
steps: Lie on your back with your arms extended out to the sides and your legs straight. This will be your starting position.
Lift one leg and quickly cross it over your body, attempting to touch the ground near the opposite hand.
Return to the starting position, and repeat with the opposite leg. Continue to alternate for 10-20 repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms extended out to the sides and your legs straight. This will be your starting position. Lift one leg and quickly cross it over your body, attempting to touch the ground near the opposite hand. Return to the starting position, and repeat with the opposite leg. Continue to alternate for 10-20 repetitions.

name: Yoke Walk
steps: The yoke is usually done with a yoke apparatus, but is sometimes seen with refrigerators or other heavy objects.
Begin by racking the apparatus across the back of the shoulders. With your head looking forward and back arched, lift the yoke by driving through the heels.

Begin walking as quickly as possible using short, quick steps. You may hold the side posts of the yoke to help steady it and hold it in position. Continue for the given distance as fast as possible, usually 75-100 feet.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

With your head looking forward and back arched, lift the yoke by driving through the heels. Begin walking as quickly as possible using short, quick steps. You may hold the side posts of the yoke to help steady it and hold it in position. Continue for the given distance as fast as possible, usually 75-100 feet.

name: Chair Figure-Four Stretch
steps: Sit tall on a sturdy chair with both feet flat on the floor.
Lift your right leg and rest your right ankle across your left knee, creating a 'figure-4' shape.
Keep your right foot lightly flexed to protect your knee joint.
With your spine tall and chest lifted, gently hinge forward from your hips until you feel a comfortable stretch in your outer right hip.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing calmly, then return upright and repeat on the other side.
coaching_cues: Hinge forward from your hip crease rather than rounding through your spine.
Do not press forcefully down on your raised knee.
Ideal for breaking up long periods of sitting at a desk.
instructions: Sit tall on a sturdy chair with both feet flat on the floor. Lift your right leg and rest your right ankle across your left knee, creating a 'figure-4' shape. Keep your right foot lightly flexed to protect your knee joint. With your spine tall and chest lifted, gently hinge forward from your hips until you feel a comfortable stretch in your outer right hip. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing calmly, then return upright and repeat on the other side.

name: Chair Sit-to-Stand

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: CDC STEADI Fall Prevention & NIH Senior Health

steps: Sit on the front half of a sturdy, armless chair with your feet flat on the floor, about shoulder-width apart.
Cross your arms over your chest or hold them extended straight in front of you for counter-balance.
Lean slightly forward from your hips, keeping your chest proud and spine long.
Push firmly down through your heels to rise smoothly to a full, balanced standing position.
Hinge your hips back and bend your knees to lower yourself gently back onto the chair under control without plopping down.
coaching_cues: Do not rock back and forth to gain momentum; stand using leg strength alone.
Make sure your knees stay aligned over your second toes and do not cave inward.
Keep your eyes focused forward on the horizon.
instructions: Sit on the front half of a sturdy, armless chair with your feet flat on the floor, about shoulder-width apart. Cross your arms over your chest or hold them extended straight in front of you for counter-balance. Lean slightly forward from your hips, keeping your chest proud and spine long. Push firmly down through your heels to rise smoothly to a full, balanced standing position. Hinge your hips back and bend your knees to lower yourself gently back onto the chair under control without plopping down.

name: Bench Copenhagen Plank

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: British Journal of Sports Medicine Copenhagen Adductor Protocol

steps: Lie on your side next to a sturdy low bench or chair, resting on your bottom forearm.
Place the knee and lower leg of your top leg on top of the bench.
Rest your bottom leg on the floor beneath the bench.
Press through your top knee and forearm to raise your hips off the floor into a side plank, lifting your bottom leg to hover just beneath the bench.
Hold this rigid line for the target duration, feeling your inner thigh work strongly, then lower with control.
coaching_cues: Beginners should start with the bench supporting from the knee (short lever) rather than the ankle.
Keep your shoulders and hips square without rotating toward the floor.
Breathe calmly and evenly throughout the hold.
instructions: Lie on your side next to a sturdy low bench or chair, resting on your bottom forearm. Place the knee and lower leg of your top leg on top of the bench. Rest your bottom leg on the floor beneath the bench. Press through your top knee and forearm to raise your hips off the floor into a side plank, lifting your bottom leg to hover just beneath the bench. Hold this rigid line for the target duration, feeling your inner thigh work strongly, then lower with control.

name: Step Eccentric Heel Drop
steps: Stand with the balls of both feet on the edge of a sturdy step or stair, holding the handrail or wall for balance.
Rise up onto the toes of both feet.
Transfer all your weight onto the target leg (e.g., right foot).
Slowly lower your right heel down below the level of the step over a count of 3 to 4 seconds, loading the Achilles tendon eccentrically.
Place your left foot back on the step and use both feet to rise back up to the top, repeating the eccentric lowering on the target leg.
coaching_cues: The magic of the Alfredson protocol is the slow eccentric lowering; use both feet to push back up.
Perform with both straight knee (gastrocnemius) and slightly bent knee (soleus).
A mild ache during the stretch is expected, but avoid sharp, unbearable pain.

name: Towel Roll Quad Set
steps: Sit on the floor or a firm bed with your target leg extended straight and opposite knee bent.
Place a small rolled towel or washcloth directly under the knee of your target leg.
Tighten your thigh muscles and press the back of your knee firmly down into the towel roll.
Hold the hard isometric quad contraction for 5 full seconds while feeling your kneecap pull upward.
Relax completely for 2 seconds, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions.
coaching_cues: Focus on driving the back of your knee into the towel to activate the vastus medialis oblique.
Do not hold your breath during the 5-second hold; breathe steadily.
Ensure your heel stays in contact with the mat throughout.
instructions: Sit on the floor or a firm bed with your target leg extended straight and opposite knee bent. Place a small rolled towel or washcloth directly under the knee of your target leg. Tighten your thigh muscles and press the back of your knee firmly down into the towel roll. Hold the hard isometric quad contraction for 5 full seconds while feeling your kneecap pull upward. name: Step Lateral Step-Down

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: Cornell Health Lower Extremity Strengthening Protocol

steps: Stand tall on top of a low step or box (about 4 to 6 inches high) with your target leg bearing your weight on the edge.
Let your non-target leg hover freely off the side of the step.
Hinge your hips slightly back and bend your standing knee, slowly lowering your body until your hovering heel lightly taps the floor.
Keep your standing knee tracking straight over your second toe without caving inward.
Push through your standing heel to return to the starting position.
coaching_cues: Do not put weight onto the foot tapping the floor; merely graze it like touching thin ice.
Keep your hips square and do not let your pelvis tilt or drop.
Lower slowly over a 3-second count to load the quadriceps eccentrically.
instructions: Stand tall on top of a low step or box (about 4 to 6 inches high) with your target leg bearing your weight on the edge. Let your non-target leg hover freely off the side of the step. Hinge your hips slightly back and bend your standing knee, slowly lowering your body until your hovering heel lightly taps the floor. Keep your standing knee tracking straight over your second toe without caving inward. Push through your standing heel to return to the starting position.

name: Step Forward Step-Up

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: Cornell Health Lower Extremity Strengthening Protocol

steps: Stand facing a sturdy low step or platform (4 to 8 inches high) with feet hip-width apart.
Place your entire right foot firmly onto the step.
Press down through your right heel to lift your body up, bringing your left foot onto the step beside your right.
Step backward with your left foot to the floor, followed by your right foot.
Repeat the movement leading with your left foot.
coaching_cues: Do not push off with your trailing back foot; make the lead leg do the work of lifting your body.
Keep your torso upright with your chest proud and eyes forward.
Ensure your whole foot is planted securely on the step before pressing up.
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy low step or platform (4 to 8 inches high) with feet hip-width apart. Place your entire right foot firmly onto the step. Press down through your right heel to lift your body up, bringing your left foot onto the step beside your right. Step backward with your left foot to the floor, followed by your right foot. name: Bolster Short Arc Quad
steps: Lie on your back on a firm, comfortable surface with a foam roller or rolled bolster placed horizontally under your target knee.
Allow your heel to rest on the floor with your knee bent at roughly a 20 to 30 degree angle over the bolster.
Keeping the back of your knee resting against the bolster, slowly straighten your lower leg by contracting the quadriceps on the front of your thigh.
Extend the knee until your leg is fully straight and your heel lifts completely off the floor.
Hold the straight-leg contraction for 3 to 5 seconds, focusing on squeezing the vastus medialis just above your knee.
Slowly lower your heel back down to the floor with control.
coaching_cues: Do not lift your thigh or knee off the bolster; keep the back of the knee anchored to isolate terminal extension.
Keep your toes pointed straight up toward the ceiling throughout the movement.
Contract your thigh muscles firmly at the top without hyperextending violently.
instructions: Lie on your back on a firm, comfortable surface with a foam roller or rolled bolster placed horizontally under your target knee. Allow your heel to rest on the floor with your knee bent at roughly a 20 to 30 degree angle over the bolster. Keeping the back of your knee resting against the bolster, slowly straighten your lower leg by contracting the quadriceps on the front of your thigh. Extend the knee until your leg is fully straight and your heel lifts completely off the floor. Hold the straight-leg contraction for 3 to 5 seconds, focusing on squeezing the vastus medialis just above your knee. Slowly lower your heel back down to the floor with control.

name: Backward Medicine Ball Throw
steps: This exercise is best done with a partner. If you lack a partner, the ball can be thrown and retrieved or thrown against a wall.
Begin standing a few meters in front of your partner, both facing the same direction. Begin holding the ball between your legs.
Squat down and then forcefully reverse direction, coming to full extension and you toss the ball over your head to your partner.
Your partner can then roll the ball back to you. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Medicine Ball Scoop Throw
steps: Assume a semisquat stance with a medicine ball in your hands. Your arms should hang so the ball is near your feet.
Begin by thrusting the hips forward as you extend through the legs, jumping up.
As you do, swing your arms up and over your head, keeping them extended, releasing the ball at the peak of your movement. The goal is to throw the ball the greatest distance behind you.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Assume a semisquat stance with a medicine ball in your hands. Your arms should hang so the ball is near your feet. As you do, swing your arms up and over your head, keeping them extended, releasing the ball at the peak of your movement. The goal is to throw the ball the greatest distance behind you.

name: Return Push From Stance
steps: You will need a partner for this drill.
Begin in an athletic 2 or 3 point stance.
At the signal, move into a position to receive the pass from your partner.
Catch the medicine ball with both hands and immediately throw it back to your partner.
You can modify this drill by running different routes.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Standing Two-Arm Overhead Throw
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart holding a medicine ball in both hands. To begin, reach the medicine ball deep behind your head as you bend the knees slightly and lean back.
Violently throw the ball forward, flexing at the hip and using your whole body to complete the movement.
The medicine ball can be thrown to a partner or to a wall, receiving it as it bounces back.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

Violently throw the ball forward, flexing at the hip and using your whole body to complete the movement. The medicine ball can be thrown to a partner or to a wall, receiving it as it bounces back.

name: Barbell Front Raise
aliases: Standing Front Barbell Raise Over Head
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
Keep your arms straight and lift the barbell forward and upward until it reaches shoulder level.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip. Keep your arms straight and lift the barbell forward and upward until it reaches shoulder level. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell One Arm Snatch
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outwards.
Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and lower your hips into a squat position, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles, driving the barbell upwards.
As the barbell reaches chest level, pull it upwards with your arm, keeping it close to your body.
Rotate your elbow under the barbell and extend your arm fully overhead, locking out your elbow.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outwards. Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees and lower your hips into a squat position, keeping your back straight and chest up. Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles, driving the barbell upwards. As the barbell reaches chest level, pull it upwards with your arm, keeping it close to your body. Rotate your elbow under the barbell and extend your arm fully overhead, locking out your elbow. Lower the barbell back down to the starting position in a controlled manner. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

name: Barbell Rear Delt Raise
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Raise the barbell out to the sides, keeping your arms straight, until they are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight. Raise the barbell out to the sides, keeping your arms straight, until they are parallel to the ground. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Pull the barbell towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up. Pull the barbell towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Seated Behind Head Military Press
steps: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell off the rack and bring it down to shoulder level, behind your head.
Press the barbell upward until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion

steps: While standing upright, hold a barbell plate in both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions. Your palms should be facing each other and your arms should be extended straight out in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by rotating the plate as far to one side as possible. Use the same type of movement you would use to turn a steering wheel to one side.

name: Clean And Jerk
steps: With a barbell on the floor close to the shins, take an overhand or hook grip just outside the legs. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.

Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight. Move the weight with control as you continue to above the knees.

Next comes the second pull, the main source of acceleration for the clean. As the bar approaches the mid-thigh position, begin extending through the hips. In a jumping motion, accelerate by extending the hips, knees, and ankles, using speed to move the bar upward. There should be no need to actively pull through the arms to accelerate the weight; at the end of the second pull, the body should be fully extended, leaning slightly back, with the arms still extended.

As full extension is achieved, transition into the third pull by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out. At peak extension, aggressively pull yourself down, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so. Receive the bar in a front squat position, the depth of which is dependent upon the height of the bar at the end of the third pull. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed. Continue to descend to the bottom squat position, which will help in the recovery.
Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Continue until you have risen to a standing position.

The second phase is the jerk, which raises the weight overhead. Standing with the weight racked on the front of the shoulders, begin with the dip. With your feet directly under your hips, flex the knees without moving the hips backward. Go down only slightly, and reverse direction as powerfully as possible.
Drive through the heels create as much speed and force as possible, and be sure to move your head out of the way as the bar leaves the shoulders.

At this moment as the feet leave the floor, the feet must be placed into the receiving position as quickly as possible. In the brief moment the feet are not actively driving against the platform, the athletes effort to push the bar up will drive them down. The feet should be split, with one foot forward, and one foot back. Receive the bar with the arms locked out overhead. Return to a standing position.

Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

steps: This drill helps you learn to drive yourself low enough during the jerk and corrects those who move backward during the movement. Begin with the bar racked in the jerk position, with the shoulders forward, torso upright, and the feet split slightly apart.
Initiate the movement as you would a normal jerk, dipping at the knees while keeping your torso vertical, and driving back up forcefully, using momentum and not your arms to elevate the weight.
Keep the rear foot in place, using it to drive your body forward into a full split as you jerk the weight. Recover by standing up with the weight overhead.

name: Rack Delivery
steps: This drill teaches the delivery of the barbell to the rack position on the shoulders. Begin holding a bar in the scarecrow position, with the upper arms parallel to the floor, and the forearms hanging down. Use a hook grip, with your fingers wrapped over your thumbs.

Begin by rotating the elbows around the bar, delivering the bar to the shoulders. As your elbows come forward, relax your grip. The shoulders should be protracted, providing a shelf for the bar, which should lightly contact the throat.

It is important that the bar stay close to the body at all times, as with a heavier load any distance will result in an unwanted collision. As the movement becomes smoother, speed and load can be increased before progressing further.

instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the band under your feet. Hold the band handles at shoulder height with your palms facing forward. Engage your core and press the band overhead, fully extending your arms. As you press, twist your torso to one side, keeping your hips stable. Pause for a moment at the top, then return to the starting position. Repeat the press and twist on the opposite side. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Y-Raise
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the band in front of your thighs with your palms facing inwards.
Keep your arms straight and lift them up and out to the sides, forming a 'Y' shape with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the band in front of your thighs with your palms facing inwards. Keep your arms straight and lift them up and out to the sides, forming a 'Y' shape with your body. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement. Slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Band Standing Rear Delt Row
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the band under your feet.
Hold the band handles with your palms facing each other and your arms extended in front of you.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Pull the band towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight. Pull the band towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Resistance Band Seated Shoulder Press
steps: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the resistance band with both hands, palms facing forward, and bring it up to shoulder level.
Press the band overhead, extending your arms fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the band back down to shoulder level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground. Hold the resistance band with both hands, palms facing forward, and bring it up to shoulder level. Press the band overhead, extending your arms fully. Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the band back down to shoulder level. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Back Flyes - With Bands
steps: Run a band around a stationary post like that of a squat rack.
Grab the band by the handles and stand back so that the tension in the band rises.

Extend and lift the arms straight in front of you. Tip: Your arms should be straight and parallel to the floor while perpendicular to your torso. Your feet should be firmly planted on the floor spread at shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
As you exhale, move your arms to the sides and back. Keep your arms extended and parallel to the floor. Continue the movement until the arms are extended to your sides.
After a pause, go back to the original position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

Keep your arms extended and parallel to the floor. Continue the movement until the arms are extended to your sides. After a pause, go back to the original position as you inhale. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Band Pull Apart
steps: Begin with your arms extended straight out in front of you, holding the band with both hands.
Initiate the movement by performing a reverse fly motion, moving your hands out laterally to your sides.
Keep your elbows extended as you perform the movement, bringing the band to your chest. Ensure that you keep your shoulders back during the exercise.
Pause as you complete the movement, returning to the starting position under control.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Begin with your arms extended straight out in front of you, holding the band with both hands. Initiate the movement by performing a reverse fly motion, moving your hands out laterally to your sides. Keep your elbows extended as you perform the movement, bringing the band to your chest. Ensure that you keep your shoulders back during the exercise. Pause as you complete the movement, returning to the starting position under control.

name: External Rotation With Band
steps: Choke the band around a post. The band should be at the same height as your elbow. Stand with your left side to the band a couple of feet away.
Grasp the end of the band with your right hand, and keep your elbow pressed firmly to your side. We recommend you hold a pad or foam roll in place with your elbow to keep it firmly in position.
With your upper arm in position, your elbow should be flexed to 90 degrees with your hand reaching across the front of your torso. This will be your starting position.
Execute the movement by rotating your arm in a backhand motion, keeping your elbow in place.
Continue as far as you are able, pause, and then return to the starting position.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Internal Rotation With Band

With your upper arm in position, your elbow should be flexed to 90 degrees with your hand reaching away from your torso. This will be your starting position.
Execute the movement by rotating your arm in a forehand motion, keeping your elbow in place.
Continue as far as you are able, pause, and then return to the starting position.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Lateral Raise - With Bands
steps: To begin, stand on an exercise band so that tension begins at arm's length. Grasp the handles using a pronated (palms facing your thighs) grip that is slightly less than shoulder width. The handles should be resting on the sides of your thighs. Your arms should be extended with a slight bend at the elbows and your back should be straight. This will be your starting position.

Use your side shoulders to lift the handles to the sides as you exhale. Continue to lift the handles until they are slightly above parallel. Tip: As you lift the handles, slightly tilt the hand as if you were pouring water and keep your arms extended. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.
Lower the handles back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Shoulder Press - With Bands
steps: To begin, stand on an exercise band so that tension begins at arm's length. Grasp the handles and lift them so that the hands are at shoulder height at each side.
Rotate the wrists so that the palms of your hands are facing forward. Your elbows should be bent, with the upper arms and forearms in line to the torso. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, lift the handles up until your arms are fully extended overhead.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Band Shoulder External Rotation in Neutral
steps: Anchor a resistance band at elbow height.
Stand sideways to the anchor point with the target arm on the outside.
Bend your elbow to 90 degrees and hold the band handle across your belly, placing a rolled towel between your elbow and ribs.
Keeping your elbow pinned firmly to your side, rotate your forearm outward away from your body against the band's resistance.
Pause at peak external rotation for one second, then slowly return your forearm across your stomach.
coaching_cues: Keep your elbow pinned to the towel roll; do not allow your elbow to flare away from your ribs.
Maintain an upright posture and avoid twisting your torso to help move the band.
Move with smooth, steady control in both directions.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at elbow height. Stand sideways to the anchor point with the target arm on the outside. Bend your elbow to 90 degrees and hold the band handle across your belly, placing a rolled towel between your elbow and ribs. Keeping your elbow pinned firmly to your side, rotate your forearm outward away from your body against the band's resistance. Pause at peak external rotation for one second, then slowly return your forearm across your stomach.

name: Band Shoulder Internal Rotation in Neutral
steps: Anchor a resistance band at elbow height.
Stand sideways to the anchor point with your target arm closest to the anchor.
Bend your elbow to 90 degrees and hold the band handle with your forearm rotated outward away from your belly.
Keeping your elbow pinned to your side (with a small towel roll for feedback), rotate your forearm inward across your stomach.
Hold for one second against your belly, then slowly allow the band to rotate your forearm back out.
coaching_cues: Keep your wrist straight and firm without curling it as you pull inward.
Keep your shoulder blade retracted and depressed, avoiding forward rounding.
Control the return phase smoothly.

name: Band Shoulder External Rotation at 90 Degrees
steps: Anchor a resistance band at shoulder height in front of you.
Stand facing the anchor, raising your target upper arm to shoulder height abducted at 90 degrees with elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Hold the band handle with your forearm parallel to the floor.
Rotate your forearm and hand upward until your forearm is vertical and perpendicular to the floor.
Pause for one count at peak external rotation, then slowly lower your forearm back parallel to the floor.
coaching_cues: Keep your elbow fixed in space at shoulder height as the pivot point; do not drop your elbow.
Maintain an active core so your lower back does not arch as your hand rotates back.
Use a light resistance band to protect joint mechanics.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at shoulder height in front of you. Stand facing the anchor, raising your target upper arm to shoulder height abducted at 90 degrees with elbow bent at 90 degrees. Hold the band handle with your forearm parallel to the floor. Rotate your forearm and hand upward until your forearm is vertical and perpendicular to the floor. Pause for one count at peak external rotation, then slowly lower your forearm back parallel to the floor.

name: Band Shoulder Internal Rotation at 90 Degrees
steps: Anchor a resistance band at shoulder height behind you.
Stand facing away from the anchor with your target upper arm raised to shoulder height and elbow bent at 90 degrees, holding the band with forearm vertical.
Rotate your forearm forward and downward until your forearm is parallel to the floor.
Pause for one count at the bottom of the internal rotation.
Slowly rotate your forearm back up to the vertical starting position under control.
coaching_cues: Keep your upper arm level with your shoulder throughout the rotation.
Do not allow your shoulder to roll forward out of its socket at the bottom of the pull.
Maintain steady, controlled rhythm.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at shoulder height behind you. Stand facing away from the anchor with your target upper arm raised to shoulder height and elbow bent at 90 degrees, holding the band with forearm vertical. Rotate your forearm forward and downward until your forearm is parallel to the floor. Pause for one count at the bottom of the internal rotation. Slowly rotate your forearm back up to the vertical starting position under control.

name: Band Wall Walk
steps: Place a small resistance loop band around your wrists or forearms.
Stand facing a smooth wall with elbows bent at 90 degrees and forearms resting vertically against the wall at chest height.
Pull your wrists outward to create continuous outward tension on the band.
Maintaining that outward tension, slowly 'walk' your forearms upward along the wall in small alternating steps until your arms are nearly fully extended.
Walk your forearms back down in small controlled steps to chest height.
coaching_cues: Keep continuous outward tension on the band; do not let your hands cave inward.
Keep your core braced so your lower back does not arch as your hands climb higher.
Move with tiny, deliberate hand steps.

name: Rear Deltoid Stretch
steps: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your right arm across your chest, placing your left hand on your right elbow.
Gently pull your right arm towards your left shoulder, feeling a stretch in your right shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then release.
Repeat on the other side.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart. Extend your right arm across your chest, placing your left hand on your right elbow. Gently pull your right arm towards your left shoulder, feeling a stretch in your right shoulder. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then release. Repeat on the other side.

name: Left Hook. Boxing
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Keep your left hand up to protect your face and your right hand by your chin.
Rotate your hips and pivot on your left foot as you extend your left arm forward in a punching motion.
Twist your torso and engage your core muscles to generate power in the punch.
Snap your arm back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent. Keep your left hand up to protect your face and your right hand by your chin. Rotate your hips and pivot on your left foot as you extend your left arm forward in a punching motion. Twist your torso and engage your core muscles to generate power in the punch. Snap your arm back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Isometric Neck Exercise - Front And Back
steps: With your head and neck in a neutral position (normal position with head erect facing forward), place both of your hands on the front side of your head.
Now gently push forward as you contract the neck muscles but resisting any movement of your head. Start with slow tension and increase slowly. Keep breathing normally as you execute this contraction.
Hold for the recommended number of seconds.
Now release the tension slowly.
Rest for the recommended amount of time and repeat with your hands placed on the back side of your head.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions
instructions: With your head and neck in a neutral position (normal position with head erect facing forward), place both of your hands on the front side of your head. Now gently push forward as you contract the neck muscles but resisting any movement of your head. Start with slow tension and increase slowly. Keep breathing normally as you execute this contraction. Hold for the recommended number of seconds. Now release the tension slowly. Rest for the recommended amount of time and repeat with your hands placed on the back side of your head.

name: Isometric Neck Exercise - Sides
steps: With your head and neck in a neutral position (normal position with head erect facing forward), place your left hand on the left side of your head.

Now gently push towards the left as you contract the left neck muscles but resisting any movement of your head. Start with slow tension and increase slowly. Keep breathing normally as you execute this contraction.
Hold for the recommended number of seconds.
Now release the tension slowly.
Rest for the recommended amount of time and repeat with your right hand placed on the right side of your head.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Seated Front Deltoid
steps: Sit upright on the floor with your legs bent, your partner standing behind you. Stick your arms straight out to your sides, with your palms facing the ground. Attempt to move them as far behind you as possible, as your assistant holds your wrists. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your elbows straight, attempt to move your arms to the front, with your partner gently restraining you to prevent any actual movement for 10-20 seconds.
Now, relax your muscles and allow your partner to gently increase the stretch on the shoulders and chest. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Prone L-Raise
steps: Lie face down on a mat with your upper arms abducted straight out to your sides at 90 degrees.
Bend your elbows to 90 degrees so your forearms rest on the floor pointing directly forward, forming an 'L' shape.
Keeping your elbows on or slightly hovering off the floor, rotate your forearms and hands upward toward the ceiling.
Pause for one count at peak external rotation.
Slowly rotate your forearms back down until your hands gently touch the floor.
coaching_cues: Pivot strictly around the elbow axis without sliding your elbows forward or back.
Only lift as high as comfortable without any pinching in the front of your shoulder.
Perform slowly and smoothly.
instructions: Lie face down on a mat with your upper arms abducted straight out to your sides at 90 degrees. Bend your elbows to 90 degrees so your forearms rest on the floor pointing directly forward, forming an 'L' shape. Keeping your elbows on or slightly hovering off the floor, rotate your forearms and hands upward toward the ceiling. Pause for one count at peak external rotation. Slowly rotate your forearms back down until your hands gently touch the floor.

name: Wall Slide with Overhead Reach
steps: Stand with your back, head, and glutes resting flat against a smooth wall, with your feet placed about 6 inches forward.
Bring your arms up into a 'goalpost' position with your elbows and backs of your wrists touching the wall if possible.
Flatten your lower back gently toward the wall to prevent excessive arching.
Slowly slide your arms upward along the wall into an overhead reach, maintaining contact with your elbows and hands as much as comfortable.
Pause at the top of your comfortable range, then slowly slide your arms back down to the goalpost position.
coaching_cues: Do not force your wrists to touch the wall if it causes shoulder pain; stay within your pain-free zone.
Keep your ribs pulled down and avoid arching your lower back as your arms slide up.
Move with slow, deliberate control.

name: Chin Tuck

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: APTA Neck Pain Clinical Practice Guidelines

steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and gaze pointed straight ahead at eye level.
Place two fingers lightly on your chin as a tactile guide.
Without tilting your head up or down, glide your chin straight backward as if making a subtle double chin.
Feel a gentle lengthening sensation along the back of your neck and upper spine.
Hold the retracted position for 3 to 5 seconds, then relax your head back to its neutral starting position.
coaching_cues: Move your head straight back horizontally, like closing a desk drawer.
Do not nod your head down or look at your chest.
Perform multiple sets throughout the workday to counteract desk posture.

Without tilting your head up or down, glide your chin straight backward as if making a subtle double chin. Feel a gentle lengthening sensation along the back of your neck and upper spine. Hold the retracted position for 3 to 5 seconds, then relax your head back to its neutral starting position.

name: Sleeper Stretch
steps: Lie on your target side with your head comfortably supported by a pillow.
Extend your target upper arm straight out in front of your shoulder at a 90-degree angle, with your elbow bent at 90 degrees pointing your fingers toward the ceiling.
Roll your body slightly backward (about 20 degrees) so you are resting on the back of your shoulder blade, not directly on the shoulder joint.
Use your opposite hand to gently guide the wrist of your target arm downward toward the floor.
Stop at the first sensation of a gentle stretch deep in the back of your shoulder and hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
coaching_cues: Apply very gentle, steady pressure with your top hand; never force the wrist down or push through sharp pain.
The stretch should be felt in the back of the shoulder capsule, never in the front.
Breathe slowly and deeply to help the posterior rotator cuff relax.

Extend your target upper arm straight out in front of your shoulder at a 90-degree angle, with your elbow bent at 90 degrees pointing your fingers toward the ceiling. Use your opposite hand to gently guide the wrist of your target arm downward toward the floor. Stop at the first sensation of a gentle stretch deep in the back of your shoulder and hold for 20 to 30 seconds.

name: Codman Shoulder Pendulum

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: AAOS Rotator Cuff and Shoulder Conditioning Program

steps: Stand beside a sturdy table or bench and bend forward at your hips roughly 75 to 90 degrees.
Place your unaffected hand and forearm firmly on the table for full torso support.
Allow your affected arm to hang completely limp and relaxed straight down toward the floor.
Gently shift your body weight and sway your hips from side to side, forward and backward, and in small circles.
Allow the passive momentum generated by your torso rocking to swing your relaxed arm in gentle circles without engaging your shoulder muscles.
Perform clockwise circles, counter-clockwise circles, and gentle pendulum swings for the prescribed duration.
coaching_cues: The swinging arm must remain completely passive and limp; imagine it is an empty coat sleeve.
Do not actively contract your shoulder or arm muscles; let gravity and torso rocking do all the work.
Keep your neck relaxed and gaze down at the floor.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
steps: Stand or sit tall with your shoulders relaxed and pulled back.
Bring your target arm straight across your chest at upper-chest height.
Use your opposite hand to grasp your target arm just above the elbow.
Gently pull your arm closer into your chest until you feel a firm, comfortable stretch in the back of your shoulder.
Hold the stretch steady for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing normally.
Slowly release the tension and repeat on the opposite arm.
coaching_cues: Keep your target shoulder blade down and back; avoid shrugging the shoulder up toward your chin.
Do not twist your torso; keep your chest facing directly forward.
Apply gentle, consistent pressure without bouncing.
instructions: Stand or sit tall with your shoulders relaxed and pulled back. Bring your target arm straight across your chest at upper-chest height. Use your opposite hand to grasp your target arm just above the elbow. Gently pull your arm closer into your chest until you feel a firm, comfortable stretch in the back of your shoulder. Hold the stretch steady for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing normally. Slowly release the tension and repeat on the opposite arm.

name: Cervical Isometric Flexion
steps: Sit or stand tall with good posture, relaxed shoulders, and your head in a neutral position.
Place the palm of one or both hands flat against your forehead.
Gently press your forehead forward into your palm as if attempting to nod your head forward.
Simultaneously press back with your hand using equal force so your head does not move at all.
Maintain this static isometric contraction for 5 to 10 seconds while breathing normally.
Slowly release the pressure, relax for 2 seconds, and repeat.
coaching_cues: Use only moderate effort (about 30-50% maximum effort); do not strain.
Your head must remain completely still in a neutral position throughout.
Keep your shoulders down and relaxed.
instructions: Sit or stand tall with good posture, relaxed shoulders, and your head in a neutral position. Place the palm of one or both hands flat against your forehead. Gently press your forehead forward into your palm as if attempting to nod your head forward. Simultaneously press back with your hand using equal force so your head does not move at all. Maintain this static isometric contraction for 5 to 10 seconds while breathing normally. Slowly release the pressure, relax for 2 seconds, and repeat.

name: Cervical Isometric Extension
steps: Sit or stand tall with your spine erect and shoulders comfortably pulled back.
Clasp your hands together and place your palms against the back of your head (occiput).
Gently press the back of your head backward into your hands as if looking up.
Match the pressure with your hands so that no actual movement occurs.
Hold the isometric contraction for 5 to 10 seconds with steady breathing.
Gradually release the contraction and repeat.
coaching_cues: Do not tilt your head back; maintain a level chin and neutral gaze.
Apply smooth, gentle pressure without yanking.
Keep your chest open and upright.
instructions: Sit or stand tall with your spine erect and shoulders comfortably pulled back. Clasp your hands together and place your palms against the back of your head (occiput). Gently press the back of your head backward into your hands as if looking up. Match the pressure with your hands so that no actual movement occurs. Hold the isometric contraction for 5 to 10 seconds with steady breathing. Gradually release the contraction and repeat.

name: Cervical Isometric Lateral Flexion
steps: Sit tall with your shoulders relaxed and spine upright.
Place the palm of your left hand flat against the left side of your head just above your ear.
Gently push your head sideways to the left as if attempting to tilt your ear to your shoulder.
Provide equal resistance with your hand so your head stays perfectly upright and still.
Hold the static contraction for 5 to 10 seconds while breathing naturally.
Slowly release, rest for a moment, and repeat on the right side.
coaching_cues: Keep your eyes looking straight ahead and do not let your head rotate.
Avoid raising your shoulder up toward your ear to cheat the movement.
Use gentle, steady force (no more than 40% maximum effort).
instructions: Sit tall with your shoulders relaxed and spine upright. Place the palm of your left hand flat against the left side of your head just above your ear. Gently push your head sideways to the left as if attempting to tilt your ear to your shoulder. Provide equal resistance with your hand so your head stays perfectly upright and still. Hold the static contraction for 5 to 10 seconds while breathing naturally. Slowly release, rest for a moment, and repeat on the right side.

name: Cervical Isometric Rotation
steps: Sit or stand in an upright, balanced posture with your chin level.
Place your left hand on the left side of your head near your temple and cheekbone.
Attempt to turn your head to look over your left shoulder.
Use your hand to provide equal and opposite resistance, preventing any actual turning.
Hold the isometric rotation for 5 to 10 seconds while maintaining steady breathing.
Gradually release the pressure and repeat on the opposite side.
coaching_cues: The head must remain facing squarely forward throughout the contraction.
Keep your jaw relaxed and teeth unclenched.
Apply smooth, controlled pressure without jerking.

name: Low Pulley Row To Neck

Grab the ends of the rope using a palms-down grip and sit with your back straight and your knees slightly bent. Tip: Keep your back almost completely vertical and your arms fully extended in front of you. This will be your starting position.

name: Reverse Flyes
steps: To begin, lie down on an incline bench with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline. Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip).

Extend the arms in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the angle of the bench. The legs should be stationary while applying pressure with the ball of your toes. This is the starting position.

Maintaining the slight bend of the elbows, move the weights out and away from each other (to the side) in an arc motion while exhaling. Tip: Try to squeeze your shoulder blades together to get the best results from this exercise.
The arms should be elevated until they are parallel to the floor.
Feel the contraction and slowly lower the weights back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Reverse Flyes With External Rotation
steps: To begin, lie down on an incline bench set at a 30-degree angle with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline.

Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing down to the floor. Your arms should be in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the angle of the bench. Tip: Your elbows should have a slight bend. The legs should be stationary while applying pressure with the ball of your toes (your heels should not be touching the floor). Maintaining the slight bend of the elbows, move the weights out and away from each other in an arc motion while exhaling.

As you lift the weight, your wrist should externally rotate by 90-degrees so that you go from a palms down (pronated) grip to a palms facing each other (neutral) grip. Tip: Try to squeeze your shoulder blades together to get the best results from this exercise.
The arms should be elevated until they are level with the head.
Feel the contraction and slowly lower the weights back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Seated Bent-Over Rear Delt Raise
steps: Place a couple of dumbbells looking forward in front of a flat bench.
Sit on the end of the bench with your legs together and the dumbbells behind your calves.
Bend at the waist while keeping the back straight in order to pick up the dumbbells. The palms of your hands should be facing each other as you pick them. This will be your starting position.

Keeping your torso forward and stationary, and the arms slightly bent at the elbows, lift the dumbbells straight to the side until both arms are parallel to the floor. Exhale as you lift the weights. (Note: avoid swinging the torso or bringing the arms back as opposed to the side.)
After a one second contraction at the top, slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Seated Side Lateral Raise
steps: Pick a couple of dumbbells and sit at the end of a flat bench with your feet firmly on the floor. Hold the dumbbells with your palms facing in and your arms straight down at your sides at arms' length. This will be your starting position.

While maintaining the torso stationary (no swinging), lift the dumbbells to your side with a slight bend on the elbow and the hands slightly tilted forward as if pouring water in a glass. Continue to go up until you arms are parallel to the floor. Exhale as you execute this movement and pause for a second at the top.
Lower the dumbbells back down slowly to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: See-Saw Press (Alternating Side Press)
steps: Grab a dumbbell with each hand and stand up erect.

Clean (lift) the dumbbells to the chest/shoulder level and then rotate your wrists so that your palms are facing towards you as if you were getting ready to perform an Arnold Press. This will be your starting position.

Now start extending your left arm overhead as you rotate the wrist so that the palm of your hand faces forward as you go up. Your elbows should come out also as you lift the weight. Simultaneously, you will also be bending from your hip to your opposite side. Tip: If you perform the exercise correctly, is should look as if you are trying to reach for something overhead on the right hand side of your body, but with your left arm. Breathe out as you perform this movement.
Once you reach the top position breathe in. Then, with the weight fully extended overhead and you bent over to your right hand side, begin the movement to the left side.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
coaching_cues: Maintain controlled form throughout the entire range of motion
Avoid using momentum to complete repetitions

name: Side Lateral Raise
steps: Pick a couple of dumbbells and stand with a straight torso and the dumbbells by your side at arms length with the palms of the hand facing you. This will be your starting position.

While maintaining the torso in a stationary position (no swinging), lift the dumbbells to your side with a slight bend on the elbow and the hands slightly tilted forward as if pouring water in a glass. Lower the dumbbells back down slowly to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
